domains.label: Native fields, coefficient carriers and Cartan comparison
domains.summary: The four-colour native theory has an intrinsic ordered source, a global Cartan isomorphism and an actual marked field evaluation through \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\) at fixed noncritical level. The source and its topology are defined independently of that evaluation. Explicit state, Ward and completion results determine which stronger comparisons still need construction.

domains.label: Currents, sewing and endpoint duality
domains.summary: Actual finite current operations, geometric Ward sewing and endpoint dualities are constructed in specified algebraic, formal, Laurent and smooth domains. Their stronger comparisons retain the full input actions, supported attachments, collision boundaries and completion choices.

domains.label: Centres, exterior sources and genuine actions
domains.summary: Exterior-source mapping spaces, tame base change and genuine actions are different comparisons. The source theorem is complete for one odd generator; the full Heisenberg actor comparison retains an independent coverage and evaluation problem.
conventions: All vertex algebras and tensors in this section are ordinary algebraic objects over C unless a statement says otherwise.

A roof presents a derived map by a state quasi-isomorphism on one leg and an actual morphism on the other. Tameness means that the full ideal generated by the image of the relevant base kernel is acyclic.
The genuine Heisenberg comparison uses nonzero level and retains the specified unit homotopy. A source-space equivalence alone does not identify that recipient.

domains.label: Two-colour actions and canonical vacua
domains.summary: Full recognition is established for canonical chiral Chevalley actors, including unbounded states and unrestricted vertex translation. General actor primitives, full relative recipients, coherent roots and marked-cut comparisons retain their exact pointing and source domains.

domains.label: Quantum fields and their module categories
domains.summary: Corrected induction, reflected duality and local quantum fields are compared on their actual algebraic or completed carriers. The elliptic construction now has all-order fields matching a precise native prefix, alongside finite higher fields and compatible moment systems.

domains.label: Analytic sewing and free elliptic reduction
domains.summary: Completed sewing, representing recipients and singular current comparisons are established on their stated sources. The remaining categorical and relative-cubic questions concern the exact maps and input domains needed to join those constructions.

domains.label: Native gravity, stress operations and prepared states
domains.summary: Actual source and normal-operation comparisons, finite native integrals and analytic Gaussian limits, with the remaining physical cap and stress dictionary stated on their original domains.

domains.label: Induction and source localization
domains.summary: Ordinary source units, native realization and their exact localizations.

domains.label: Unframed augmentations and critical mapping spaces
domains.summary: Transverse augmentation and underlying coalgebra mapping have different answers at critical level. The transverse simple-family locus is exact, while the underlying critical sl2 zero-character fibre contains distinct components even after its entire central character is fixed. A full Koszul extension calculation identifies which displayed components can extend.

claims.title: Native coefficients and their independent recipient
claims.statement: For the four-colour native system over \(R_3=\mathbb C[\hbar]/(\hbar^3)\), the coefficient derivative identity holds at every exterior length, jet order and numerical level. Its second-order exterior differential operator has order at most three, and the generator-left quadratic and cubic ghost rows are explicit. The independent covariant recipient \(Q=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(M,\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(V,V((u))))[-1]\) has both rooted actions, marked degree \(1-n\) and a scalar-vacuum dg retract. Whole-carrier marked evaluation at fixed noncritical level is supplied by a separate theorem.
hypotheses: All four colours, ordinary Koszul signs and algebraic state inputs are retained. Combined kernels are formed before coincident-germ substitution.
The exterior-operator order bound is not a rooted Taylor-arity bound; generator-left products do not assert arbitrary composite-left products.
claims.sourceLabel: All-monomial native derivative; binary and ternary kernels; covariant dg recipient

claims.title: A marked evaluation on the completed ordered source
claims.statement: At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm ten}=\mathcal P+\mathcal J+\Xi\), with \(\Xi=d_Q\mathcal H+\mathcal H d_{\rm ten}\), is an actual continuous dg bimodule evaluation for the full smooth native algebra. It is defined on every homogeneous element of the ordered polynomial marked carrier and its specified restricted Laurent extension. It has both coefficient-indexed Ward laws and transports through the finite and global Cartan isomorphisms.
hypotheses: The source is pointwise Hom on algebraic inserted CE inputs, with arbitrary completed left current values and exact RTT-pullback right-module quotients.

In the polynomial carrier, each inserted input has one finite Laurent interval across all right slices. In the Laurent carrier, each fixed right slice and inserted input has one Laurent floor, one ghost cutoff and one finite right PBW support for the entire series.
The recipient consists of Laurent-valued maps on algebraic inserted and rooted states. Trace currents and trace ghosts are retained.
This is a particular checked evaluation; identification with the full prescribed physical right adjoint and full physical \(R_2\) normalization are separate.
claims.sourceLabel: All-marked tensor evaluation, Theorems 6.1 and 7.1, Lemma 8.1 and Section 9

claims.title: An intrinsic ordered rooted carrier
claims.statement: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_3\), the ordered source \(N^{1-n}=\varprojlim_R\operatorname*{colim}_L(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}((G/J_L)^n,A)\otimes_{R_3,\mathrm{alg}}A_R)\) is a continuous dg bimodule over the full smooth native algebra \(A\). Both completed endpoint actions, translation and the scalar chain augmentation are defined. Finite expressions have a canonical dense map into this carrier.
hypotheses: \(A_R=A/\zeta^{-1}(I_R^D)\) is the exact free RTT-PBW left-module quotient under the native-to-RTT comparison \(\zeta\); it is not a quotient algebra.
At each right slice there is one upper ghost cutoff and finite right PBW support. The middle functions may take arbitrary completed values in \(A\).
The dense map is not an assertion of injectivity or purity of an abstract endpoint tensor product.
claims.sourceLabel: Ordered rooted carrier, Proposition 3.1, Theorem 4.1 and Section 5

claims.title: Finite Cartan frames and a genuine coefficient output
claims.statement: At every numerical level over \(R_3\), the pointwise Laurent-polynomial marked carrier is a dg full-\(A\) bimodule. Every finite Cartan cutoff gives an actual continuous frame isomorphism with its full second-order composition and prescribed native mixed rows. The separate coefficient output \(C\), its balanced Laurent augmentation and the trace-retaining restriction \(\alpha_{\rm tr}\) are genuine dg constructions. At fixed \(K\ne-2\), the coefficient pullback has a direct dg section and contractible restriction kernel; its projection to the marked source is a quasi-isomorphism.
hypotheses: Each algebraic inserted input has a globally finite Laurent interval. Ghost cutoffs and finite right support may vary with the right slice.
The coefficient output is \(C=N[1]\otimes_{A_{\rm alg},\mathrm{alg}}W\); its balancing uses finite-word Ward equivariance. Completed currents act on individual algebraic output coefficients.
The section uses the noncritical algebraic state retract and finite state precomposition. Its quasi-isomorphism is the coefficient pullback projection, not the augmentation \(N[1]\to A\).
claims.sourceLabel: Marked carrier and restriction, Sections 1–5; noncritical coefficient-section lemma

claims.title: The additional condition for a scalar-normalized section
claims.statement: The optional coefficient section can be corrected to give the whole scalar field if its domain also has a free closed scalar middle summand, an endpoint-linear projection onto that summand, and a compatible closed full-field coefficient lift. The correction can change prescribed rooted values, so agreement with the chosen rooted homotopies still needs a separate comparison.
hypotheses: Fixed finite Cartan cutoff and fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\).
The extra free-summand projection and endpoint extension are not supplied on the global completed source by the coefficient-section theorem.
This condition concerns the separate coefficient section; it is not a remaining premise of the independently checked direct marked evaluation.
claims.sourceLabel: Noncritical coefficient-section lemma, optional scalar hypothesis; marked carrier Section 5

claims.title: A global Cartan isomorphism with uniform Laurent bounds
claims.statement: At every numerical \(K\) over \(R_3\), the restricted Laurent source has an actual continuous Cartan operator \(T=\lim_M T_M\). Its composition \(T^2\) defines strict inverse frame maps \(\Gamma^{\pm1}=1\pm\hbar T+\tfrac12\hbar^2T^2\). The resolved differential is the limit of the prescribed native rows and equals \(\Gamma d_{\rm ten}\Gamma^{-1}\). Both total and relative translation commute with the global frame map.
hypotheses: The rooted source is \(\varprojlim_R\operatorname*{colim}_L(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}((G/J_L)^n,A)((u))\otimes_{R_3,\mathrm{alg}}A_R)\); the marked source is pointwise Hom on algebraic inserted inputs.
One Laurent floor, one ghost cutoff and finite right PBW support work across the entire series at each fixed right slice and inserted input. These bounds may vary between slices and inputs.
Relative translation is \(\partial_u^{\rm src}F-FT_B\); total translation is \(T_{\rm rt}F-FT_B\). Bare \(\partial_u^{\rm src}\) is not substituted for the relative operator.
claims.sourceLabel: Global Cartan carrier, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 and equations (6.13)–(6.14)

claims.title: Pure-root values extend to the ordered completion
claims.statement: At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), the chosen finite pure-root evaluation extends uniquely and continuously to every rooted degree of the ordered carrier. The extension is a dg full-\(A\)-bimodule map, preserves both Ward laws and all prescribed scalar, first-root and native quadratic values, and retains the full algebraic trace factors. Its restricted Laurent version has finite coefficient convolution; the global source theorem supplies its chain and total-translation domain conditions.
hypotheses: At a right slice annihilating the rooted input, one ghost cutoff \(L\) and finite right support are fixed. For root degree \(n\), inserted weight bound \(W\), and weight bound \(D\) on the finite right-translated input list, the kernel floor is \(-nL-W-D-2\).

A Laurent coefficient family also has one floor \(\nu\) across the whole series at that slice. Its output floor is at least \(\nu-nL-W-D-2\); endpoint multipliers are constant completed elements of \(A\).
The higher gauge is that of the finite transfer. Equality with separately fixed lexicographic higher values is not asserted.
claims.sourceLabel: Ordered pure-root evaluation, Theorems A and B; uniform Laurent corollary

claims.title: Second-order inserted and mixed transport
claims.statement: At every numerical level over \(R_3\), the prescribed inserted homotopy and exact correction have actual Cartan-transported values on inserted-one, inserted-two, inserted/rooted-one and bare-root-one cells. Their cofinal Laurent limits satisfy the specified combined native differential rows. The second coefficient retains both mixed orders and the action on the newly created inserted factor, with every native cross term through order \(\hbar^2\).
hypotheses: Common enlarged finite paired coefficient presentations and algebraic state inputs are used.
The affine-linear Cartan row acts by native currents; replacing it with the full native current commutator would change the second-order formula.
Preserved pure-root values are on Cartan-normalized tensor cells. The bare-root correction is additional data.
claims.sourceLabel: Inserted and mixed transport, equations (8) and (12)–(24)

claims.title: The evaluation keeps the field and its fixed normalizations
claims.statement: For the checked noncritical \(R_3\) marked evaluation, the scalar value is the whole field, and every prescribed first-root homotopy and the full native \(q_\hbar\) column survive. The classical oriented \(H[1]\wedge H[-1]\) value on \(q\) is \(4/u\). Positive inserted cycles take \(q_\hbar\) to \(-\mathrm{id}\) and \(\omega_\hbar\) to \(+\mathrm{id}\). The inserted Casimir and first mixed values retain their prescribed native terms and trace phases.
hypotheses: Fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\), algebraic trace-current states and finite trace-ghost degree.
After frame transport, the normalization is evaluated on \(\Gamma\)-normalized tensor cells.
claims.sourceLabel: All-marked tensor evaluation, Section 10

claims.title: Literal coefficient restriction does not give the evaluation
claims.statement: The direct marked evaluation differs from \(\epsilon_C\alpha_{\rm tr}\). For the signed trace root \(r_{I,0}^{\rm Ch}=-r_{c^I_{-1}}^{\rm raw}\) with unit endpoints, their values on the same finite-frame source and trace-ghost test are \(-\mathrm{id}\) and zero. A raw singleton would give \(+\mathrm{id}\), so the sign convention matters. Agreement on scalar and ghost-free trace-current states does not supply a factorization.
hypotheses: Fixed finite Cartan cutoff, fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) and \(R_3\).
Both maps are compared on \(\Gamma_Mr_{I,0}^{\rm Ch}\) in the resolved marked source; the inserted current is the vacuum and the ghost is \(\xi_0^I\).
claims.sourceLabel: All-marked tensor evaluation, corrected Section 10 witness

claims.title: The original finite-word carrier is not a complex
claims.statement: The ordinary algebraic finite-word endpoint tensor is not stable under the native differential: the \(H[0]\wedge E[0]\) row has infinitely many surviving middle coefficients. The ordered carrier admits that differential, but its dense finite-expression image is still not a subcomplex. This distinguishes the replacement carrier from the failed original.
hypotheses: The stated ordinary coefficient tensor, full native \(R_3\) differential and all four colours are retained.
The conclusion concerns differential stability of this carrier, not all possible completed sources or physical realizations.
claims.sourceLabel: Decorated pullback required repair; ordered rooted carrier, Section 6

claims.title: A common ghost cutoff is necessary for these extensions
claims.statement: Coefficientwise membership in the ordered source is insufficient for its Laurent extension. If the ghost cutoff may grow with the exponent, the explicit Cartan example has a retained coefficient proportional to \(M-1\), and the pure trace-root example has evaluation coefficient \(-(M+1)u^{-1}\). Allowing a separate Laurent pole bound at each ghost coordinate also defeats the pure contraction. These arrays lie outside the checked uniform domain.
hypotheses: The source-Cartan example holds at every numerical level over \(R_3\); the pure-evaluation examples use its fixed noncritical state scope.
The counterexamples retain the specified coefficient tests and topology. They do not exclude different recipients or the original full physical comparison.
claims.sourceLabel: Global Cartan carrier, Section 7; uniform Laurent corollary, excluded-domain examples

claims.title: Finite projected coefficients form a valid prodiagram
claims.statement: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_3\), the normalized finite free closed complexes with basis \(u^te j_t\), \(0\le t<T\), have actual images \(u^t(1\otimes X_H(-t-1))e\) in the checked carrier. The projections commute with right-quotient transitions and truncation of the nonnegative Laurent coefficients below exponent \(T\).
hypotheses: \(e\) is the closed marked scalar and \(j_t\) is the normalized rooted letter dual to \(c_t^H\).
This is a morphism of finite coefficient diagrams. The ordinary inverse limit is not identified with the prescribed physical source.
claims.sourceLabel: Fixed-word, fixed-weight projection boundary, finite prodiagram

claims.title: The ordinary inverse limit exceeds finite right support
claims.statement: The finite projection has no coefficient-preserving ordinary-inverse-limit value in the checked global carrier. Its required series has infinitely many independent right PBW coordinates already at the first right quotient modulo \(\hbar\), while that carrier requires finite right support across the whole series. The witness has fixed word length, degree and conformal weight, Laurent floor zero and a common scalar middle cutoff. Its scalar-vacuum state series is nevertheless a legitimate Laurent series.
hypotheses: Every numerical \(K\), over \(R_3\), with target scalar slice \(A((u))\otimes_{R_3,\mathrm{alg}}A_R\).
Every finite Laurent coefficient must agree with the specified projection.
The finite prodiagram survives. No universal obstruction to physical evaluation or to all recipients follows.
claims.sourceLabel: Fixed-word, fixed-weight projection boundary, Proposition

claims.title: The noncritical native state complex has a small retract
claims.statement: At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), the actual states \(1,q_\hbar,\omega_\hbar\), with \(dq_\hbar=2T\omega_\hbar\), sit in a translation-linear strong deformation retract retaining all trace-current polynomials and trace ghosts. Ordinary state cohomology is \((R_3\mathbf1\oplus R_3[\omega_\hbar])\otimes L\), with no extra \(\hbar\)-torsion. Precomposition gives the corresponding shifted-Hom dg bimodule retract.
hypotheses: All states are algebraic. Input weights through \(W\) require only weights through \(W+2\).
\(L\) is the full algebraic trace factor. No critical or uniform-in-level contraction is asserted.
claims.sourceLabel: Native state strong deformation retract, Theorem 2 and Section 5

claims.title: Relative Ward cohomology retains the full trace factor
claims.statement: At fixed \(K\ne-2\), let \(\mathcal Z_p=\ker(\partial_u-(-)T_L)\) on \(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(L^p,\mathcal E)\), with \(\mathcal Z_p=0\) for \(p<0\) and \(\mathcal E=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(V,V((u)))\). Then \(H^m(Q_{\rm rel})\cong\mathcal Z_{1-m}\oplus\mathcal Z_{-2-m}\oplus\delta_{m,-1}\mathcal E_{\rm const}\). Only the scalar trace state contributes the separate \(q_\hbar\)-residue obstruction.
hypotheses: \(R_3\), algebraic native states and full algebraic trace input; Laurent truncation is pointwise. \(Q_{\rm rel}\) is the relative-Ward subcomplex of the covariant recipient \(Q\).
This is relative Ward cohomology. It does not by itself show that a proposed source forcing is defined, closed or Ward.
claims.sourceLabel: Full trace relative Ward cohomology

claims.title: A conditional test for relative Ward primitives
claims.statement: An already defined closed relative-Ward forcing of degree \(-1\) has a relative-Ward primitive precisely when its value on \(1\otimes L^2\) and its scalar-trace residue on \(q_\hbar\otimes1\) vanish. In degree \(-2\), the tests are its values on \(1\otimes L^3\) and \(\omega_\hbar\otimes L^0\); there is no additional residue test on every trace state. Ordinary exactness is weaker: the difference between the prescribed classical \(4/u\) quadratic value and the contraction primitive has residue \(4\,\mathrm{id}\) and is not a relative-Ward boundary.
hypotheses: Fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\), \(R_3\), full algebraic trace factor and the stated relative-Ward recipient.
Definedness, closedness and the relative Ward condition of the actual forcing are hypotheses. Total Ward and physical normalization require their own comparison.
claims.sourceLabel: Full trace primitive criterion; native residue detector

claims.title: Third values and fourth representative tests in a fixed gauge
claims.statement: For the separate fixed lexicographic higher gauge at noncritical \(R_3\), an actual third pure-root value solves its native chain equation. The fourth forcing vanishes on both complete degree-three state-cohomology representative families. These statements do not identify the fixed higher values with the different gauge used by the all-degree transfer.
hypotheses: Fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\), common finite coefficient enlargements, algebraic states and full trace factors.
Global closedness and a fourth filler in this specific gauge remain additional.
claims.sourceLabel: Actual third pure-root value; fourth-rooted representative test

claims.title: What the fourth representative tests imply
claims.statement: If the fourth forcing in the fixed lexicographic gauge is globally closed, its vanishing on the complete degree-three state-cohomology representatives and the native state retract imply that its ordinary shifted-Hom obstruction class is zero. The separate all-degree transfer does not supply that hypothesis for this fixed gauge.
hypotheses: Fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), the original lexicographic lower choices and full algebraic trace factor.
Global closedness of this particular forcing must be supplied.
claims.sourceLabel: Fourth-rooted representative test, conditional obstruction consequence

claims.title: Critical quadratic primitives exist at all algebraic weights
claims.statement: At \(K=-2\), every actual signed quadratic pure-root forcing with the prescribed first homotopies annihilates every algebraic native degree-one cycle. It therefore has an individual ordinary \(R_3\)-linear primitive with the stated pointwise Laurent bound, in every algebraic weight. The all-weight classical generation theorem and the full trace factor are included.
hypotheses: Actual native \(R_3\) states, including algebraic lifts with arbitrary finite high-weight \(\hbar\)-corrections.
For adjusted degree \(d\), inserted weight \(\alpha\) and rooted-input weight \(b\), the bound is \(t\ge-\alpha-b-d-2\).
These are individual ordinary primitives, not a coherent critical Ward-compatible evaluation.
claims.sourceLabel: Critical all-weight generation and native quadratic integration

claims.title: State ghost lifting and the trace-retaining quotient
claims.statement: For every numerical level over \(R_3\), the state ghost inclusion is an algebraic translation-linear chain map, polynomial in the level, retaining the native unit, \(q_\hbar\), \(\omega_\hbar\), descendants and trace ghosts. It has a graded left inverse. At each fixed noncritical level, the trace-retaining state quotient has an actual square-zero contraction.
hypotheses: Input weights through \(W\) require only \(W+2\).
The all-level graded inverse is not asserted to be a chain map. The quotient contraction is fixed-level noncritical and retains all trace currents.
claims.sourceLabel: State ghost lift and noncritical trace quotient

claims.title: The coupled canonical quadratic/cubic residual is solved
claims.statement: The native operators satisfy \(\mathscr D Z_q=2\partial_u Z_\omega\) and \(\mathscr D Z_\omega=0\). The coupled fixed-frame residual equations have explicit solutions at every numerical level, including zero and critical level, on the declared finite-composition domain and its separating smooth structural coefficient hull. The source gauges retain the prescribed first term and the mixed second-order term with coefficient one; both Ward laws and strict rooted units hold.
hypotheses: \(R_3\), finite inserted polynomials with all trace jets, finite structural expression trees and the stated cutoff-dependent Laurent bounds.
The smooth-module comparison uses its actual module variation; it does not impose a common vacuum-style inner drift on every module.
The represented canonical comparison is distinct from a physical marked right-adjoint identification or a continuous inverse from fields.
claims.sourceLabel: Native quadratic operator; coupled canonical residual; smooth canonical transport

claims.title: Current, curved-bar and separated-point carriers
claims.statement: The full smooth native and RTT current algebras agree through \(R_3\). At every finite precision, a complete curved bar carrier and polarized bar module have intrinsic translation; their strict native polarized quotient comparison is supplied through precision three. Independently, the classical two-point Ward and all-precision two-site RTT carriers have exact module quotients and finite sections. Their completed root projections are noninjective.
hypotheses: The separated-point statements invert the separation parameter and retain the declared PBW quotient topologies.
The polarized quotient section is only continuous and linear; no module, chain or translation compatibility of the section is asserted.
These are carrier and current comparisons. They do not supply the nonlinear native field comparison on arbitrary smooth two-point sums.
claims.sourceLabel: Smooth current comparison; complete polarized bar module; two-point Ward and RTT carriers

claims.title: Finite field coefficients separate finite state spans
claims.statement: For every numerical level over \(R_3\) and every finite number of fields, the native ordered field tensor is injective and has a finite coefficient left inverse on each finite state span. The concrete finite-word current algebra acts by a Ward representation respecting its operator relations. The prescribed first rooted homotopies have exact relative and total translation laws.
hypotheses: Finite state support is taken over ordered Laurent scalars, with detecting inverses chosen on finite complex state spans. No uniform bound across infinite support or faithfulness of the entire completed current algebra is inferred.
The first-root statements use actual algebraic states and the independently defined Laurent-valued recipient.
claims.sourceLabel: Finite field detection; first rooted translation

claims.title: Some prescribed smooth interchanges fail
claims.statement: The specified full one-point smooth completion does not continuously transport to the fixed two-point coefficient tests. A classical Ward tail gives \(4(M+1)\); an actual native relation tail gives \(2(M+1)\hbar\); and a prescribed nonlinear native-current expansion gives \(-2(M+1)\hbar\) in the RTT test while its actual native Ward value is zero. Separately, the inserted right-adjoint factor has a nonstabilizing coefficient proportional to \(M\).
hypotheses: Every numerical level, with the exact stated smooth topologies and retained coefficient detectors; native tails are through \(R_3\).
The independently constructed separated carriers, stabilized total current action and admitted smaller source domains remain valid. The conclusions do not rule out every realization.
claims.sourceLabel: Smooth Ward obstruction; native relation and nonlinear-current tail detectors; inserted Cartan bridge

claims.title: Strict comparison obstructions retain their hypotheses
claims.statement: The prescribed fixed-pairing \(R_2\) ghost-algebra comparison is obstructed by the native anticommutator. At noncritical level, the fixed native product also admits no continuous strict \(R_3\)-algebra isomorphism with continuous inverse to an associative \(R_4\) lift on the stated common coefficientwise split carrier. Larger resolutions, noninvertible or higher comparisons and changes of the classical map are not excluded by these results.
hypotheses: The first statement concerns a parity-preserving strict unital map from RTT ghosts to native ghosts at every level, with classical values \(a_s^*=-c_s\) and \(b_r^*=c_{-r}\) fixed.
The second assumes \(K\ne-2\), the original native product, a common coefficientwise splitting and the specified strict continuous inverse.
claims.sourceLabel: Fixed-pairing obstruction; strict split-flat comparison obstruction

claims.title: The stronger physical and operation comparison
claims.statement: The remaining physical target is to identify the checked carrier and evaluation with the prescribed full marked right adjoint, impose its full \(R_2\) and unit-relative normalization, and compare native ordered products, supported residues, collisions and tensorators on the required domains. Full right-dual and merged-mode completion, coefficient biduality, completed bar/cobar comparison and compatible higher precision require separate constructions.
hypotheses: The ordered source, global Cartan isomorphism and actual noncritical marked evaluation are already established on their stated domains.
The target retains both genuine endpoint actions, distinct unit and vacuum data, full trace factors and the prescribed supported operations.
claims.sourceLabel: All-marked tensor evaluation, final scope

claims.title: Coherent critical evaluation remains a separate target
claims.statement: Critical level has individual ordinary quadratic primitives at every algebraic weight. A coherent critical choice satisfying the required Ward laws, higher source equations and physical normalizations is still separate from the noncritical all-marked construction. Unrestricted families of ordinary Hom corrections need not even define an admissible Laurent-valued correction.
hypotheses: \(K=-2\), actual native \(R_3\) state and coefficient domains.
The all-weight existence statement for each individual quadratic primitive is retained.
claims.sourceLabel: Critical native quadratic integration and its admissible correction domain

claims.title: Native currents retain their full coefficient space
claims.statement: At each fixed finite particle number, the parameter-proper joint-current carrier has a typed completed-projective kernel inverse. Native moments are quasi-isomorphisms at every closed external support, with bounded lifts on each stage and support-preserving choice homotopies. The full three-position cohomology retains the three escaping coefficient modules and forest classes.
hypotheses: On each external compact retain one compact coefficient carrier, eventual collar height and finite joint distribution-order bound.
Native coefficient space E_n is the symmetric analytic-functional coefficient space; use every closed external support.

claims.title: Actual relative quotients and admitted contact operations
claims.statement: Selected bulk/ray quotients agree under the original current complex with their two-image and six-image contact cofibres, with full finite jets retained. Independent squarefree marked stars and the specified repeated-ray relative quotient contract. For the explicitly admitted local operation family, the supported ideal has an algebraic cofiber comparison to the quotient; the stated low-degree, Laurent and escaping classes are retained.
hypotheses: Finite polynomial state coefficients and finite holomorphic jets; the selected relative condition is additional to the collar condition.
Marked stars use squarefree independent normals. Repeated-ray quotients use one bulk endpoint, one polynomial state endpoint and a fixed independent outer sheet.
The operation-ideal comparison applies only to the explicitly admitted label-retaining local operations with actual typed domains and differential relations; particle sums remain algebraic.
Numerical Laurent comparisons use nonzero level; integral zero fibres remain separate.

claims.title: The actual contact telescope reaches full coefficients
claims.statement: For fixed finite particle number n, the algebraic annular contact telescope has six full analytic-functional coefficient modules in degree two. At nonzero level its actual inclusion into the full triple-supported relative complex is a normal-linear quasi-isomorphism, and the induced cofiber agrees with the geometric quotient under the original current complex. The earlier polynomial contact cones and their stated markings remain embedded.
hypotheses: E_n=(O(C^n)′_b)_{S_n}; P=P_s⊗P_v; the Banach moment stages have cofinal radii and disjoint annular representatives.
The numerical comparison assumes κ≠0. The integral comparison uses algebraic extension over A=C[hbar] and hbar-weighted actual images.
All normal poles, state inputs and sums over annular stages are finite; bounds are stagewise, and root/cutoff changes transport the auxiliary data.

claims.title: Polynomial contacts and full coefficients differ
claims.statement: At nonzero level the polynomial six-contact comparison is an equivalence in the vacuum sector n=0 and fails for n≥1. Its discrepancies are six principal-part modules with coefficient quotient E_n/V_n: four in the first-cohomology cokernel and two forest modules in the second-cohomology kernel. The full geometric quotient retains the three escaping coefficient cokernels.
hypotheses: Retain full analytic-functional coefficients E_n and polynomial subspace V_n.
The full-support quotient is extra geometric data, not inferred from the collar or the whole native operation ideal.

claims.title: The zero deformation fibre retains Tor
claims.statement: Over C[hbar], the telescope inclusion acts by multiplication by hbar on its six full coefficient modules. Its comparison cone has the quotient by hbar in degree one, and the derived zero fibre has the six modules in degrees zero and one. Replacing derived base change by the images formed only after specialization erases these classes.
hypotheses: E_n=(O(C^n)′_b)_{S_n}; P=P_s⊗P_v; the Banach moment stages have cofinal radii and disjoint annular representatives.
The numerical comparison assumes κ≠0. The integral comparison uses algebraic extension over A=C[hbar] and hbar-weighted actual images.
All normal poles, state inputs and sums over annular stages are finite; bounds are stagewise, and root/cutoff changes transport the auxiliary data.

claims.title: A separated spectator changes supported cohomology
claims.statement: On the specified four-position proper-triple tube with a separated complex spectator, locally finite two-normal coefficient families have an additional Dolbeault cokernel. Two detected forest modules inject into ambient degree-three cohomology, and the full supported quotient kills exactly that detected image. This statement does not exhaust the ambient degree-three cohomology.
hypotheses: D is a connected complex disc with dist(D,0)>2epsilon; Z is exactly the three mixed pair diagonals for labels 1,2,3 and H=H₁₂₃, with label 4 retained.
L_P(D) consists of coefficient families locally finite on spectator compacts, not an unrestricted product or a globally finite normal sum; E_P(D)=coker(dbar:L_P⁰→L_P¹).
The scalar vacuum is a strict retract of the finite-particle parameter-proper native complex. The enlarged Ward domain is the explicitly displayed locally finite family of finite physical state jets.

claims.title: The admitted Ward domain controls the escaping classes
claims.statement: At nonzero level, a differential contact-image complex containing both specified locally finite Ward images has a cofiber that kills the two detected scalar-vacuum escaping modules. If the image instead lies in the globally finite-normal supported complex, the old degree-three cohomology injects into its cofiber. These conclusions depend on the actual admitted input domain.
hypotheses: D is a connected complex disc with dist(D,0)>2epsilon; Z is exactly the three mixed pair diagonals for labels 1,2,3 and H=H₁₂₃, with label 4 retained.
L_P(D) consists of coefficient families locally finite on spectator compacts, not an unrestricted product or a globally finite normal sum; E_P(D)=coker(dbar:L_P⁰→L_P¹).

claims.title: Surjective transitions identify the tame subcategory
claims.statement: For a surjective base arrow \(a:d\to d'\), let \(I_g\) be the dg vertex ideal generated by \(h(\ker a)\). claims.title: Self-linking is fixed by the charge
claims.statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(A=V_\kappa\), \(\kappa\ne0\), and \(B=\Lambda(\epsilon)\), with \(|\epsilon|=1\) and \(d\epsilon=T\epsilon=0\), using ordinary algebraic tensors. On a full unit-preserving roof, permissible lifts satisfy \(dz=0\), \(dw=Tz\), \(dv=w_{(0)}z\), with \(v\) in the acyclic kernel. The scalar \(f(v)=\operatorname{sl}(\alpha)\mathbf1\) is independent of the lift choices and all roof refinements. A full-roof self-bracket identity proves \[\operatorname{sl}(\alpha)=\frac{\operatorname{ch}(\alpha)^2}{2\kappa}\] on every genuine exterior-actor component, without nilpotent, energy-bounded, split or cofibrant source restrictions. For any quasi-isomorphic resolution target \(i:A\to W\), the same scalar multiple of the vacuum is \(H^0(i)^{-1}[f(v)-f(w)_{(0)}y]\), where \(dy=f(z)\), with all source and target links retained. The specific projected singular-bracket tuple formed from these lifts and their kernel primitives admits the normal form \[(F,\mathcal B,\mathcal V,\mathcal R)=(\gamma J+\beta\mathbf1,\kappa\gamma\mathbf1,\tfrac12\kappa\gamma^2\mathbf1,0),\qquad\gamma=\operatorname{ch}/\kappa,\quad\beta=\operatorname{ct},\] after an allowed path-roof enlargement. Choice/refinement-invariant functions solely of this tuple cannot distinguish components with the same charge and translation pair. This does not classify regular-product constructions or all binary coherent data, and does not make that pair complete. This self-linking detector supplies no third component parameter or obstruction to the image of \(q_B\) on components. Injectivity and surjectivity of \(q_B\) on components, its actual fibres and higher homotopy, full base transitions, the nilpotent inclusion and \(\lambda_B\) remain open. The displayed ternary kernel primitives exist, but their invariance and values are not established.

One has \(H^0(I_g)=Q\), \(H^1(I_g)=\epsilon Q\) and \(\Theta=0\), with both an outgoing projection and an incoming surjective tame refinement. Another has \(S=C_B\otimes\mathbb C[z,dz]\), \(I_g=C_B\otimes\mathbb C[z]dz\) and \(\Theta=A\). It has no outgoing arrow to a tame object, while the constructions below give incoming tame refinements. Its three specified old lifts remain non-tame; this does not exclude other lifts. For \(K=\ker p\), the full subcategory satisfying \(K_{(m)}I_g=0\) for every integer \(m\) has a natural incoming refinement \(S\ltimes_p(B\otimes N)\to S\), with an additional \(B\) factor and generated ideal exactly \(B\otimes N\). The bounded current/jet domain is also not preserved by every original algebraic horizontal map.
hypotheses: Use the specified u-adic source topology and ordinary finite-normal recipient; the result includes zero charge support.
Other topologies, changed recipients and restricted continuous morphisms are not excluded.
claims.sourceLabel: Gaussian completion, unrestricted gauge and residue obstructions

claims.title: Completed symbols have their own coherent tensor product
claims.statement: The independently defined column-completed balanced symbolic tensor has an explicit inverse tensorator, both moment actions, forced shifts and finite coherence. Its full formal action is faithful. At zero Gamma it preserves and reflects the uniform hbar-adic filtration, including infinite state rank.
hypotheses: Use the specified column completion and symbolic coefficient algebra with unrestricted algebraic state support.
The zero-Gamma filtration assertion and the zero-state case are separate from the nonzero-Gamma limitations.
claims.sourceLabel: Column-finite matrix symbols, completed symbolic tensor theorem

claims.title: Faithfulness does not identify every continuous operator
claims.statement: For nonzero Gamma and nonzero state space, finite-stage symbolic actions are not faithful, and the inverse of the full faithful action is not continuous in the stated uniform topology. With a nontrivial Cartan base, a continuous coordinate derivative is an explicit operator outside the symbolic image.
hypotheses: Keep the specified symbolic completion and uniform topology.
The assertions do not replace the full formal faithfulness theorem or classify operators on a different completion.
claims.sourceLabel: Column-finite matrix symbols, finite-stage and operator-image obstructions

claims.title: Independent periods act between moment frames
claims.statement: At the stated local analytic coefficient scope, independent marked-point lattice transport is constructed between chart-and-sign-frame moment objects. It preserves both base actions, finite balanced-tensor coherence, units and state translation, and transports normal derivatives, residues and coefficient extraction on the labelled divisors.
hypotheses: Both bases use the same scalar pullback. Localization and the chosen Laurent order at intersections are retained.
The transport can change the left moment sign frame; it is not an independent-period action on one fixed total-Cartan moment object.
claims.sourceLabel: Cartan-frame independent periods, transport and finite-normal statements

claims.title: The fixed-moment exchange has a nonzero detector
claims.statement: An ordinary right-base-linear native exchange preserving the same specified left moment has the order-hbar² obstruction −[H_total,R1]. The detector remains a nonzero meromorphic germ in all four sign frames. A simultaneous or changing-frame period transport does not erase this fixed-moment obstruction.
hypotheses: Keep the original single Cartan base, moment system and ordinary right-base-linearity requirement.
This is a nonzero germ, not a claim of pointwise nonvanishing at every spectral value. Shifted arrows, different moment systems and nontrivial tensor constraints are not excluded.
claims.sourceLabel: Finite normals and framed periods, fixed-moment exchange detector

claims.title: Finite normal operations keep their coefficient domains
claims.statement: Finite scalar normal operations commute with the balanced comparisons in the specified single-coefficient normal forms. Their two Laurent recipients retain their separate state-support conditions and a lower Laurent bound at each formal order.
hypotheses: The statement concerns the declared normal form, localization and finite transfer order.
It is not a factorwise operation on every presentation of an arbitrary balanced tensor.
claims.sourceLabel: Finite normal transfers, scalar coefficient comparison

claims.title: The old determinant filtration obstruction keeps its scope
claims.statement: With hbar fixed, the divided determinant relation excludes the simultaneous degree-one RTT filtration, closed filtration pieces, torsion-free completed associated graded and classical symmetric carrier with the usual entry symbols. This does not obstruct the distinct determinant-free source and its completed Rees construction.
hypotheses: The divided determinant relation, entry symbols and degree-one weights are fixed.
Nonlinear coordinates, changed weights, parameter scaling and other two-parameter lattices are outside the obstruction.
claims.sourceLabel: Fixed-hbar degree-one RTT filtration, necessary-condition obstruction

claims.title: The full common-category comparison remains stronger
claims.statement: The local elliptic field theorems and the typed rational, KZ and Gaussian instances still need the full common native comparison with genuine mixed tensors, independently defined colour-operation spaces, their multiplicative Ward map and the prescribed supported cut and unit maps. Selected integral lattices, global field-period comparison, recognition and analytic or physical sewing are further specified comparisons.
hypotheses: Keep each proved source category, recipient, marking and morphism class.
A supplied Ward field, a coend or a local all-order field algebra is not by itself the requested independent universal operation comparison.
claims.sourceLabel: Final scope of the actual native quintic realization and the mixed supported, rational and marked KZ instances

claims.title: Five channels on the full ordered interior
claims.statement: The five independently sewn positive-input channel germs have compatible completed continuations over the logarithmic bidisc 0<|x|,|y|<1, with z1=xy and z2=y, and hence over 0<z1<z2<1. Four entire-energy inputs are admitted, with one sufficient finite Hilbert source stage on each compact configuration set and one fixed regularized output. Both internal spectra, the output spectrum and all descendant levels remain uncut. The extreme nested tree has raw inverse-Gram convergence on this bidisc; the other four retain their own raw sewing domains.
hypotheses: Real c>1; fixed positive principal input labels; normalized boundary hypothesis H, the established analytic estimates and the normalized spectral-label pentagon.
The finite source exponent may depend on the compact configuration set; no uniform estimate at the collision boundary is asserted.
claims.sourceLabel: Full-interior five-point comparison

claims.title: Every placement of one vacuum input
claims.statement: The canonical mixed sewings, their middle and endpoint constructions, and their reflected comparisons cover all four positions of one vacuum input. They admit full entangled sources, retain all levels and spectra, and satisfy the coefficient-one unit triangles on the admitted stages. The outer vacuum field takes the sharp three-positive-input output into a fixed strictly negative energy stage. The left unit includes its coordinate translation, and every channel keeps its own two-binary normalization.
hypotheses: Real c>1, positive principal labels, inherited H and canonical analytic estimates.
Use the specified rapid vacuum source, strengthened to V_sigma at the endpoints; restriction to the mode-stable graph source uses its identity seminorm.
Comparisons may concern analytically continued maps when a direct overlap is empty.
claims.sourceLabel: Canonical, middle and endpoint mixed-sewing theorems

claims.title: Full rational Ward identities for the mixed maps
claims.statement: Every rational vector field with poles at the four inputs and infinity acts on the complete mixed graph source, and the actual sewn maps satisfy its Ward identity in one fixed negative-energy output space. This includes arbitrary entangled inputs and the normally convergent local germ series. All four vacuum placements have these identities throughout the real ordered interior and on local complex neighbourhoods.
hypotheses: Real c>1; positive principal input labels A,B,C; the original graph vacuum G with q_D(omega)=||D omega||_V_sigma for every finite Virasoro word D; positive entire-energy factors E_X=intersection_n H_X[n].

The actual canonical N and end-vacuum E maps, canonical measure m_b, binary mark 2^(1/4)sqrt(C_0), normalized vacuum vertex, boundary hypothesis H, and the accepted two-sided and end-vacuum estimates remain hypotheses.
Output Z[s]=L2(dm(k)dm(e);H_e[s]) retains k as unweighted spectral multiplicity. Local germs have finite principal parts and uniform holomorphic family bounds on compact parameter sets.
For all placements the output exponent tau exceeds log(1+exp(max(lambda_1,0))), where lambda_1 is the canonical two-sided output threshold.
claims.sourceLabel: FW.1-FW.5

claims.title: The exact continuation condition
claims.statement: A tree comparison transports the completed rational Ward identities on a connected continuation domain when the retained-label unitary is independent of position, preserves the final label, and the continued maps have locally stronger output bounds and uniform source-germ bounds. The outgoing series also requires max_i log+|a_i|<tau for the fixed final output exponent tau. Beyond that position bound, a simple pole field can already have outgoing terms that fail to tend to zero.
hypotheses: The output is Z[-tau], with a locally stronger stage Z[-tau_0], 0<tau_0<tau.
The negative assertion concerns the unrestricted normally convergent outgoing-series claim; it does not invalidate the normalized interior comparison.
claims.sourceLabel: FW.5 and its exact continuation scope

claims.title: Completed vacuum Ward quotients
claims.statement: The mode-stable vacuum graph is a complete Frechet source for all finite-principal-part meromorphic germs. On the specified smooth compact spectral sources, the trivalent quotients with one, two and three vacuum legs are respectively the test-function space on the positive spectrum, zero and the scalar field. The nonzero quotients split by normalized primary sections and represent continuous Ward forms into Hausdorff locally convex targets.
hypotheses: Fix real c>1 and the original rapid vacuum and graph topologies.
The spectral sources are smooth and compactly supported; this is not an assertion about arbitrary spectral distributions.
claims.sourceLabel: Completed trivalent vacuum and graph-source theorems

claims.title: The vacuum graph is nuclear
claims.statement: The original mode-stable vacuum graph is nuclear. Adjoining the raising word L_-2 D to a finite set of graph words gives trace-class maps between the actual Hilbert graph completions, and a cofinal increasing system of such norms retains exactly the original topology.
hypotheses: Fix c>1 and the irreducible unitary vacuum module V=sum_N V_N with L0=N.
Use sigma_0=1 and sigma_N=2^(3N)exp(N^2)M_N, where M_N>=1 is nondecreasing, and the original complete graph topology q_D(omega)=||D omega||_V_sigma.
For a finite graph-word set F containing the identity, H_F is the completion in p_F^2=sum_(D in F)q_D^2; F+=F union {L_-2 D:D in F}.

claims.title: The full mixed array source is a projective tensor
claims.statement: The actual fourfold graph-array space is canonically G completed-projective-tensor E_A completed-projective-tensor E_B completed-projective-tensor E_C. Every entangled array is included. It is nuclear, and each array has a decomposable series absolutely convergent in every projective seminorm. The binary positive entire-energy source likewise equals its full coefficient-array Hilbert intersection.
hypotheses: Fix c>1 and positive principal labels A,B,C; retain exactly the original vacuum graph G and positive entire-energy spaces E_X.
F4 uses the actual coefficient arrays and seminorms ||(D tensor exp(nL0_A) tensor exp(nL0_B) tensor exp(nL0_C))u||, with the vacuum weight applied after D.
Use the accepted trace-class strengthening of the actual vacuum graph norms.
claims.sourceLabel: TP.1-TP.4, including TP.3a

claims.title: Descendant traces and two independent endpoint radii
claims.statement: Formal descendant torus traces admit Serre-derivative reconstruction with modular coefficient covectors; at inserted level N only Fourier orders through floor(N/12) are required. The actual compact-insertion trace theorem has Gaussian control of the uncut traced momentum. The vacuum trace extends this control across compact charge intervals that may cross c=25. Two independently chosen strict endpoint radii then give canonical integrated norms, and the finite-rational-family argument extracts every canonical fibre with Gaussian decay.
hypotheses: The principal-insertion trace theorem keeps c in a compact subset of (1,25), the inserted label in a compact positive set and the nome in a compact subset of (0,1).
The vacuum trace, two-radius and canonical-fibre assertions retain H and their strict source margins; vacuum charge compacts lie in (1,infinity).
Canonical fibre extraction is a theorem about the actual normalized family, not point evaluation of arbitrary spectral L2 sections.
claims.sourceLabel: Serre reconstruction, descendant traces and canonical two-radius estimates

claims.title: A common representing recipient for fixed inputs
claims.statement: For two fixed positive point-module inputs, the closed common carrier represents the declared full rational Ward operations into the Gaussian-growth section recipient, positive spectral strong duals, the meromorphic recipient, the vacuum graph dual, and closed invariant subspaces of arbitrary products of these targets. The morphisms are ordinary continuous Virasoro intertwiners. The common carriers themselves are admitted targets, and actual energy dilations use the same carrier at every nonzero logarithmic coordinate.
hypotheses: Real c>1 and the retained component construction hypotheses, including H where used.
Inputs remain E_a completed-projective-tensor E_b for fixed a,b>0.
Admitting a carrier as a target does not make every vector of it an admissible input to a subsequent sewing.
claims.sourceLabel: D.1-D.4 and E.2-E.3

claims.title: The enlarged Gaussian target and the fixed fibres
claims.statement: The Gaussian-growth section union is complete for Cauchy nets, boundedly retractive and compactly regular. Its ordinary continuous Virasoro endomorphisms are multiplication by continuous functions of finite Gaussian growth. Its linking maps are noncompact. The fixed-Gaussian carrier maps continuously, injectively and densely to the enlarged carrier, without an asserted equality or embedding of their topologies; the older fixed-Gaussian self-target failure remains confined to its original topology.
hypotheses: Use the specified weighted C0 section stages on the positive half-line, fixed c>1 and the original charge-c fibre action.
The enlarged union and the fixed-Gaussian topology are distinct recipients.
claims.sourceLabel: Gaussian section topology and self-target factorization

claims.title: Point and meromorphic vacuum outputs
claims.statement: The smooth positive recipient admits continuous evaluation and momentum derivatives at each positive output label. The unmarked collision continues holomorphically through the vacuum momentum into its specified weak oscillator output. At fixed positive input labels, the marked meromorphic residue is the normalized vacuum operation on the diagonal and vanishes off it. The meromorphic germ recipient has its own residue universal property; comparison with the graph-dual vacuum coordinate is coefficientwise and does not identify the infinite-level topologies.
hypotheses: Fix real c>1 and the retained analytic collision hypotheses and normalizations.
The meromorphic construction is at fixed input labels and on its specified germ domain; the weak oscillator and graph-dual vacuum completions stay distinct.
claims.sourceLabel: Positive point, holomorphic boundary and meromorphic residue theorems

claims.title: Joint spectral testing has a logarithmic vacuum limit
claims.statement: Joint testing across the positive diagonal produces a separate complete logarithmic recipient. On the stated closed right sectors, the leading term is sqrt(epsilon) log(1/epsilon) times the coefficient-one diagonal vacuum operation, with the prescribed spectral measure. The fixed-label meromorphic germs do not form a continuous family in one common germ space across that diagonal. The logarithmic recipient splits as a locally convex space, but its residue sequence does not split as Virasoro modules.
hypotheses: Retain the specified weak-output sector topology, compact spectral tests, admitted energy stages and actual-boundary hypotheses.
The diagonal limit uses the displayed logarithmic renormalization; the raw joint amplitude tends to zero.
claims.sourceLabel: Joint logarithmic vacuum recipient

claims.title: The exact spectral cap threshold
claims.statement: On the weighted Neumann-cosine scale over a compact positive spectral interval, the coefficient-one scalar cap is continuous on the Hilbert tensor source exactly when s+t>1/2 for s,t>=0. The corresponding descendant cap retains its rapid vacuum norm and admitted energy stages. The cap is also continuous on the specified projective tensor and smooth spectral test sources.
hypotheses: Use the specified weighted Neumann-cosine Hilbert spaces and canonical positive spectral measure.
The descendant statement retains the completed mixed Ward bounds; the scalar threshold is exact.
claims.sourceLabel: Spectral-cap source theorem

claims.title: Energy regularity alone does not support the cap
claims.statement: The coefficient-one cap has no continuous extension to the energy-only Hilbert tensor source or to its entire-energy intersection. Smooth compact ground-level packets already witness the failure. This does not contradict bounded bilinearity or projective-tensor continuity, and it does not by itself obstruct a category with a different admissible source.
hypotheses: The compact positive interval has nonempty interior, and the energy seminorms do not control spectral derivatives.
claims.sourceLabel: Spectral-cap source theorem

claims.title: Separate input actions are controlled on the source
claims.statement: On the completed projective tensor of two positive entire-energy modules, finite polynomial vector fields approximate each separate regular input mode with geometric error after one source-seminorm strengthening. Every closed linear subspace invariant under the joint regular action therefore inherits the separate regular actions.
hypotheses: Fix c>1, a,b>0 and z nonzero; E_ab=E_a completed-projective-tensor E_b with the entire-energy Frechet topologies.
Use the actual charge-c source action Delta_z(L_n)=L_n(a) tensor 1 + sum_j binom(n+1,j)z^(n+1-j)1 tensor L_(j-1)(b), with finite sum for n>=-1.
The subspace K is closed and linear and invariant under every regular joint mode n>=-1.

claims.title: Regular covariance detects the whole completed source
claims.statement: A continuous linear map from the positive entire-energy tensor source to a Hausdorff locally convex target is injective if it intertwines all regular joint modes and has nonzero highest-input image. Separate source energy projections detect a nonzero finite-bidegree component, and the regular input actions then detect the highest tensor. Linearity is necessary for this criterion.
hypotheses: Fix c>1, a,b>0 and nonzero logarithmic coordinate z; source E_ab is the exact completed projective tensor of the two entire-energy modules.
For KI.2, W is Hausdorff locally convex, A_n are continuous operators for n>=-1, and F:E_ab to W is explicitly continuous and linear, with F Delta_z(L_n)=A_n F and F(v_a tensor v_b) nonzero.
claims.sourceLabel: KI.1-KI.2 with continuous linear F

claims.title: Actual positive collisions lose no source vector
claims.statement: The actual common, Gaussian, meromorphic, fixed-positive-point and strict integrated collisions are injective on the positive entire-energy tensor source under their construction hypotheses. Any nonempty open positive spectral interval still detects the entire input. The equal-label graph-dual vacuum operation is injective as well. These are injectivity conclusions, without an inverse or an identification of source and recipient-induced topologies.
hypotheses: Fix c>1, a,b>0 and nonzero logarithmic coordinate z; source E_ab is the exact completed projective tensor of the two entire-energy modules.
For KI.2, W is Hausdorff locally convex, A_n are continuous operators for n>=-1, and F:E_ab to W is explicitly continuous and linear, with F Delta_z(L_n)=A_n F and F(v_a tensor v_b) nonzero.

The applications to actual collision components retain their established analytic hypotheses H, normalization, regular covariance, and nonzero primary coefficients. Integrated outputs use every strict real stage s<-log|z|.
claims.sourceLabel: KI.3 under the retained actual-map hypotheses

claims.title: Completed quotients have exact tensor kernels
claims.statement: For Frechet spaces E,F and closed subspaces K,L, the completed projective tensor of the quotient maps is an open surjection with kernel closure(K tensor F + E tensor L). The factorization property holds for every Hausdorff locally convex target, and all finite reassociations and orders of taking closed quotients agree. Nuclearity is unnecessary.
hypotheses: All spaces are over the same real or complex field.
E,F are Frechet spaces; K subset E and L subset F are closed linear subspaces. Quotients have their locally convex quotient topologies.
All tensor products are completed projective tensor products; finite-factor coherence is asserted only for a finite number of factors.
claims.sourceLabel: Closed quotients of completed projective tensor products, assertions 1-4

claims.title: Proper annular sources support actual finite sewing
claims.statement: For a fixed Gaussian Banach source stage, sufficiently long annular preparation gives actual canonical sewing on full entangled fields, with absolutely convergent spectral integrals and descendant contractions. The bare preparation threshold is strict; a collision kernel with its own Gaussian decay can include its endpoint. Finite chains admit compatible energy margins, and one annulus can be chosen uniformly on each bounded source subset. These source-dependent statements retain the propagated, scaled input modes.
hypotheses: Use one specified Gaussian Banach stage B_n and the retained canonical kernel estimates.
Bare preparation into the energy-r target requires tau>n+r; the kernel-assisted estimate permits tau>=n+r.
For successive seams the sufficient energy bridge is tau_(i+1)+v_i>=r_(i+1). These are finite-chain, stage-dependent domains.
claims.sourceLabel: Canonical input-domain and stage-dependent sewing theorems

claims.title: The actual common output cannot be the whole next input
claims.statement: The actual fixed-output outer primary sewing cannot extend continuously to every vector of the common recipient, even after any one fixed finite incoming annulus. Its forced scalar negative-mode coefficients grow linearly at the outer puncture, whereas the common recipient has a convergent negative-mode series there. The actual complete cluster quotient source still carries the sewing continuously and maps densely into the recipient with its finer topology.
hypotheses: Fix c>1, A,B,C,e>0, 0<z<1 and a nonzero nonnegative chi in C_c^infinity((0,infinity)) in the retained label k.

Use the actual complete common recipient R^G_AB with its established continuous Virasoro modes and entire negative-mode series, the canonical measure m_b, two-binary mark sqrt(2)sqrt(C_0(A,B,k)C_0(k,C,e)), and inherited H and analytic assumptions.
The final label e is a fixed point label. The continuous test is chi(k)Omega_e^vee; no arbitrary evaluation of an integrated L2 output at e is used.
claims.sourceLabel: OS.1-OS.4

claims.title: The remaining comparison is an input-source category
claims.statement: The stronger objective is a compatible test-source assignment for arbitrary recipient objects, actual binary operations on those sources, stability under repeated sewing, and identification of the associator and unit maps with the sewn maps. Fixed-input representability, all-placement fixed-source unit triangles, mixed rational Ward covariance and the nuclear tensor-source structure are available. Their coexistence does not supply the arbitrary-object construction.
hypotheses: The desired source assignment must retain the declared topology, charge-c actions, normalization and actual sewing domains.
The whole-recipient obstruction concerns one inadmissible input choice; proper quotient and annular sources remain possible.
claims.sourceLabel: Arbitrary-recipient source and monoidal realization problem

claims.title: Incoming relations and an independent graph realization
claims.statement: For the chosen labelled cubic matching with two occurrences of root U and one of root V, the incoming relation cylinder descends to the actual current image with its full source differential. The independent graph-current and central-bar realization has actual Wick operations and a square-zero differential before trace. The fixed-branch polynomial-to-supported normal comparison supplies its ordered cubic source inverse; these constructions retain the individual branches and central outputs.
hypotheses: Use the original eight incoming faces, all declared finite jets and anchor choices, and the specified branch-indexed normal diagrams.
The independent graph construction, the native normal comparison and the compact marking are distinct maps.
claims.sourceLabel: Incoming relation cylinder, independent graph and normal-source bridge

claims.title: All sixteen histories on the polynomial-Thom carrier
claims.statement: Complete root-and-central collar matrices construct all sixteen cubic histories on the specified polynomial-Thom graph-first carrier. The resulting untraced transferred operation has its own source chain equation. Finite prisms for all subsets of the six scalar contact coordinates retain their face identities, normal connections, support and excess factors. Scalar repeated-root vanishing holds on its stated exterior-degree-zero domain.
hypotheses: Use the generated polynomial-Thom source, original anchors, finite jets and distinct central elliptic outputs.
The repeated-root scalar result has exterior degree zero and finite induced jets; it does not evaluate every tuple-changing history.
claims.sourceLabel: Compact-history core and higher coordinate prisms

claims.title: Actual first-order source and contact prisms
claims.statement: On the evaluated graph-marked scalar root and finite-jet domain, the native first residue equals its independent counterpart. The first-order source comparison and its full cone retain both source rows and the localization and coordinate endpoint terms. The specified first-contact primitive and radial lower-section regularizations have actual open, proper-pair and point current limits.
hypotheses: Keep the original coefficient differential, supported correction and the exact scalar-root finite-jet domain.
These first-order statements do not construct the independent quadratic primitive or the full lower marking.
claims.sourceLabel: First-order source bridge and first-contact trace

claims.title: A nonzero fourth-order current can have zero trace
claims.statement: The original one-field normal collar has controlled current limits on the anchored three-covariance word. Its displayed bare compact-partner alpha kernel has a strictly positive fourth moment and an untraced point current of exact order four, with coefficient M/2, although its proper central-base trace is zero. Weighted Green-leg alpha terms retain a nonzero commutator correction; their vanishing cannot be inferred from the unweighted case.
hypotheses: The exact-order and nonzero claims use the specified unweighted zero-jet bare kernel, not every higher-jet or anchor combination.
The original native normalization and suspension sign are restored separately.
claims.sourceLabel: Single-field collar and positive fourth-moment theorem

claims.title: The first transverse normal family is realized
claims.statement: Finite q-smooth strong-current families admit the actual finite normal relation projection, compatible with the full differential and both normal Weyl actions. On the first ordered transverse family u_v tensor v_w, every exterior row, finite jet and q-independent branch face satisfies the normalized canonical-current comparison.
hypotheses: Use smooth families in the real coordinates of q in C^2, valued in the specified strong-current stages, with finite sigma degree, the prescribed other normal jets and the full original coefficient differential; this is not the space of arbitrary joint currents.

The relation projection is P=r exp(-partial_q partial_sigma), with r the family value at q=0 killing positive dbar-q degree, and P kills positive contact-exterior degree. Its Taylor sum is finite; q-dependent multipliers stay inside that operation. The fixed scalar normalization is C=(4pi^2)^(-1).
The realized input is the first ordered u_v tensor v_w family, with q-independent branch faces and the full exterior complex; no unidentified native chart is assumed.
claims.sourceLabel: Proposition T.1 and the first ordered transverse family

claims.title: One supported field has its own current limit
claims.statement: Replacing one field by its signed supported section, with its matching unweighted radial primitive and four remaining top Thom fields, gives the stated limits in all three pair positions. The eta and s limits and the g rows vanish, while the c_t alpha point order is at most 4+J+q. The displayed bare supported-prefix moment obeys M_sp>M_sm>0, has coefficient M_sp/2 and exact order four, and retains zero proper central trace at its declared coefficient scope.
hypotheses: Use the original labelled cubic matching with roots U,U,V, all original anchor choices, one signed supported field and its matching unweighted radial primitive; the other four fields remain original top Thom fields.
All three positions of the selected pair are admitted with the stated finite designated and coefficient jets. Positive field-normal weights before Green are excluded.
The moment and zero-trace assertions have the explicitly stated bare or normal-independent coefficient scope.
claims.sourceLabel: Supported-prefix current limits and fourth moment

claims.title: A nonzero first augmented edge agrees in the prescribed order
claims.statement: The actual first augmented section edge is constructed with all designated raw pair jets, the complete central Taylor correction, its normal primitive and both prism vertex legs. Native and independent section edges agree and are nonzero when the order and contraction agree. Reversing the order retains an intersection projector and a source term; those terms cannot be discarded before identifying the fixed lower comparison.
hypotheses: Use the actual prescribed first augmented section edge on s_U,ell, all designated raw pair jets, coefficient boundaries, and the full central Taylor correction.
Keep both prism vertex legs, the intersection support projector, and every fixed-t0 source term, including trace-free central inputs.
Native and independently projected edges are compared only at the same prescribed order and contraction.
claims.sourceLabel: First augmented branch edge with its order addendum

claims.title: The singular supported partner is realized at fresh degree zero
claims.statement: The canonical supported-partner projection is an actual current map in all four exterior rows when the fresh incoming normal variable has degree zero. It retains every finite old-root, graph-slot and primitive-slot jet, the full boundary and the central, root and frame squares. Its zero-jet matrix is nonzero, and the first-root Taylor correction contains both 1/3 and -1/6.
hypotheses: Use the actual map rho_q^(-1) g_q^nat(C dot), C=(4pi^2)^(-1), on P(alpha,beta)A_(a;b,d) and the specified passive factors.
The fresh incoming sigma variable has degree zero. Arbitrary finite old-root, graph-slot and primitive-slot jets are retained, together with all four contact-exterior rows.
Root, retained-central and moving-frame comparisons use the displayed determinant normalizations and the unchanged original lower cochains.
claims.sourceLabel: Canonical supported-partner projection at fresh sigma degree zero

claims.title: One fully supported earlier pair is an actual single action
claims.statement: For the ordered word a1 a2 u3 v4 v5 v6, the fully supported earlier pair factors through the prescribed single root action on the independent (U,t) coefficient domain. The eta and s limits and g rows vanish, and the c_t alpha point order is at most 4+J+q. The exhibited bare fourth moment is strictly negative, with coefficient M/2 and exact order four; its proper central-base trace vanishes on the stated restricted coefficient domain.
hypotheses: Use exactly the ordered word a1 a2 u3 v4 v5 v6 with roots U,U,V: one fully supported earlier pair, one unweighted radial primitive on the second pair, and the original top third pair.
Coefficients are on the protected independent (U,t) domain and carry the prescribed single M_eta,U action. A formal second action on the same root is not used.
Retain all original anchors and finite designated/coefficient jets; the zero proper central trace has only its stated bare or normal-independent coefficient scope.
claims.sourceLabel: Earlier fully supported pair and single-action identification

claims.title: The remaining native comparison has explicit inputs
claims.statement: The supported-partner formula becomes the original native operation only after the full original-current-to-fixed-normal comparison is supplied, including tangent contraction, inverse, determinant factors and unchanged lower cochains. The root-plus-central native unit and basis matrix must also be identified; in the prescribed pure scalar normalization its factor kappa must equal one. At quadratic order, the independent source comparison additionally requires an actual primitive for the displayed residue discrepancy.
hypotheses: Use the original native current source and the fixed normal and harmonic recipients, without changing the lower maps.
Scalar tuple factors, a trace equality or the closedness of a discrepancy do not by themselves supply these comparisons.
claims.sourceLabel: Native source comparison, normalization and quadratic-prism criteria

claims.title: The full relative cubic homotopy remains to be constructed
claims.statement: The full relative cubic comparison must act on the original fixed current recipient, preserve the prescribed lower coefficients, and include the complete generated history words, branch and incidence maps, localization rows, compact endpoint and fixed lower marking. The actual normal-family, first-edge and supported-prefix results supply specific parts of that comparison. A nonzero untraced current with zero proper trace is not yet a correction-invariant obstruction to the complete homotopy.
hypotheses: The original ordered cubic cube requires its twelve u and twelve w application templates on actual after-contact families, with full coefficient boundaries and source-open terms.
Old lower equations do not extend these operations automatically to new singular families.
claims.sourceLabel: Original fixed-recipient relative cubic homotopy H3

claims.title: Finite sourced Gaussians and their full covariance
claims.statement: Formal cyclic perturbation on the original coefficient cutoff gives the moving sourced embedding, determinant, ordered Pfaffian and exact shell factors. The full stress marginal retains both the determinant ratio and covariance-difference Wick operator. The actual reference gauge also gives a finite BV heat square. Source differentiation includes the kinetic Green boundary contact; deleting a shell vacuum does not remove its covariance on higher moments.
hypotheses: Original paired coefficient cutoff, fixed input semidensity and ordered even/odd integration.
Formal smooth sources; the finite heat square uses its specified action-derived reference gauge.

claims.title: One ordinary source neighborhood for every Sobolev level
claims.statement: The actual reduced inverse exists on every ordinary \(H^s\), \(s\ge0\), and on \(C^\infty\), in one sufficiently small \(C^1\) source neighborhood. Its mixed boundary symbols and singular Green terms are retained. The paired transpose preserves the relative tangential trace without an integrability or filling hypothesis. The physical source graph still imposes its own normal-source condition.
hypotheses: Fixed smooth compact geometry and original coefficient realization.
Ordinary boundary jets; one sufficiently small C1 source neighborhood.

claims.title: The coefficient-gauge contraction needs its filling
claims.statement: For an integrable smooth source with an actual smooth Ward filling, the coefficient-gauge contraction has the stated \(H^{s+1}\to H^s\) control and chain identity. Its optional absolute normal-trace identity additionally requires the source normal trace to vanish. claims.statement: If the unary mapping space is nonempty and connected and, for every \(m\ge2\) and every base point of the full proper-unit cube, the native matching fibre is nonempty and \(m\)-connected, every specified underlying map lifts to a coherent unital transverse augmentation through a nonempty connected space of choices. The filtered criterion additionally requires its compatible vacuum-relative models and labelled native comparison; the inverse-limit argument retains its derived-limit term.

The empty-configuration unit \(K\) is distinct from the positive diagonal vacuum \(J\); the bar-cobar recipient is the entire \(U=\Omega J\).
All proper subsets, intersections and the empty vertex use the actual vacuum insertions.

claims.title: The transverse augmentation locus
claims.statement: For universal polynomial affine cochains of a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra with nondegenerate shifted form, the full ordered-atlas transverse monoid has a coherent unital augmentation through a connected space of choices. Its underlying mapping space is connected and simply connected, and every specified underlying map has a nonempty connected fibre of coherent lifts. For simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) at scalar level \(\ell\), the transverse augmentation space is nonempty exactly when \(\ell\ne-h^\vee\). Underlying critical coalgebra maps have their own nonempty mapping spaces after multiplication is forgotten.
hypotheses: The full ordered collision atlas on \(\mathbb A^1\), algebraic states and energy sums, and every output partition are retained.
The empty-configuration unit \(K\) is distinct from the positive diagonal vacuum \(J\); the bar-cobar recipient is the entire \(U=\Omega J\).

claims.title: Critical underlying maps have no transverse lift
claims.statement: For the universal polynomial affine cochain transverse monoid of a simple complex Lie algebra at \(\ell=-h^\vee\), the augmentation space is empty. The native degree-\((0,1)\) supported-pairing detector has nonzero highest normal vacuum coefficient \(h^\vee\dim(\mathfrak g)/2\). It excludes arbitrary full-envelope transverse augmentations, while leaving underlying coalgebra maps possible.
hypotheses: The full ordered collision atlas on \(\mathbb A^1\), algebraic states and energy sums, and every output partition are retained.

claims.title: Every fixed constant critical character occurs
claims.statement: For every finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra at critical level and every fixed constant vector \(c\), an actual underlying coalgebra map \(\chi_c:C_Z\to J\) exists on the full ordered atlas. Its singleton degree-zero cohomology sends \(q_{i,0}\) to \(c_i\) and all positive central jets to zero. Different constant vectors determine different connected components.
hypotheses: The full ordered collision atlas on \(\mathbb A^1\), algebraic states and energy sums, and every output partition are retained.

This gives a map for each fixed vector; it does not assert algebraic dependence of the choices on \(c\) or exhaust all components.
