claims.title: The critical original-source model and nonlinear correction
claims.statement: For critical \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), the original reduced complex has a translation-linear strong deformation retract onto \(\Omega_{>0}\oplus\eta\Omega_{>0}\oplus(\mathbb C[T]b\xrightarrow{T}\mathbb C[T]e)\), with \(|b|=2\) and \(|e|=3\). It retains the actual central and ghost representatives and has a full nonlinear Maurer–Cartan correction under the vacuum. The extension-by-zero vacuum cochain has \(R_2=R_3=0\); the specified centre-multiplicative one-form section also gives \(R_4=R_5=0\).
hypotheses: The full ordered collision atlas on \(\mathbb A^1\), algebraic states and energy sums, and every output partition are retained.
The empty-configuration unit \(K\) is distinct from the positive diagonal vacuum \(J\); the bar-cobar recipient is the entire \(U=\Omega J\).
Universal critical \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) cochains with \(q(e,f)=1\) and \(q(h,h)=2\); each reduced model term is \(\mathbb C[T]\)-free, while the vacuum is translation-torsion.

claims.title: Positive sources have a connected full mapping space
claims.statement: Let \(E=k\mathbf1\oplus M\) be a vacuum-split chiral \(L_\infty\) algebra on the affine line over a characteristic-zero field. If every \(M^d\) is free over \(k[T]\) and \(M^d=0\) for \(d<1\), with the canonical strict vacuum action, then the full derived space \(\operatorname{Map}_{J/\mathcal D}(C_E,J)\) is nonempty and connected. The positivity hypothesis is termwise on the coefficient complex, not merely on its cohomology.

claims.title: Distinct components with the same entire zero character
claims.statement: For universal critical \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) cochains, let \(\mathcal M_0\) be the homotopy fibre of central singleton restriction over the entire differential-module map \(\epsilon_0:f(q_0,q_1,\ldots)\mapsto f(0,0,\ldots)\). There are actual full-atlas points \(\chi_t\in\mathcal M_0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb C\). At any two distinct positions, the invariant \(I_{x,y}(\chi_t)=-t\) is preserved by every admitted derived homotopy. Thus \(\mathbb C\) injects into \(\pi_0\mathcal M_0\), even though the entire central character is fixed.

\(Z=\mathcal Z(\mathfrak{sl}_2,-2q)\), with \(q(e,f)=1\), \(q(h,h)=2\), and \(H^0(Z)=\mathbb C[q_0,q_1,\ldots]\). The central-restriction target is discrete.

The points are genuine all-arity maps, with all vacuum and output equations. No multiplicativity is imposed on arbitrary singleton maps in the ambient central-restriction image, and no extra symmetry condition is imposed on maps or homotopies.

claims.statement: Put \(W=Z\otimes\Lambda[\psi]\), with \(|\psi|=-1\) and \(D\psi=S\). The full mapping space \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{Map}_{J/\mathcal D}(C_W,J)\) is nonempty and connected. Restriction along the actual inclusion \(C_Z\to C_W\) has image on connected components equal to the single component of \(\chi_0\), which is also the component of the specified Koszul augmentation.

claims.title: Nonzero parameters cannot extend through the Koszul source
claims.statement: Every \(\chi_t\) with \(t\ne0\) fails to extend along \(C_Z\to C_W\), even up to homotopy. Its two-position invariant is nonzero, whereas every restriction from \(C_W\) has zero invariant. The zero-character fibre is therefore disconnected and the restriction is not surjective on connected components.

The empty-configuration unit \(K\) is distinct from the positive diagonal vacuum \(J\); the bar-cobar recipient is the entire \(U=\Omega J\).

claims.title: The full Koszul extension recurrence
claims.statement: For a specified twisting cochain \(\tau\), write \(a=\tau\pi_0\), \(D_0=\partial_0+[a,-]\) and \(B=aQ_\delta\). An extension is a solution of \(B+D_0\theta+\kappa\theta+\theta^2=0\). In exterior weight \(m\), the equation is \(D_0\theta_m=-\mathbf1_{m=1}B-\kappa\theta_{m-1}-\sum_{i+j=m,\ i,j\ge1}\theta_i\theta_j\), with \(\theta_0=0\). Its first obstruction lies in the actual global \(H^2(K_1,D_0)\); later obstructions are closed once the lower equations hold.

The compatible derived convolution model uses the algebraic exterior-degree decomposition \(\overline C_W=\bigoplus_m C^{(m)}\), with \(K_m=R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(C^{(m)},\overline U)\).
\(\pi_0\) is the graded projection, and \(Q_\delta\) comes from \(\delta\). The full \(K_1\) retains all original-source inputs, their module action, vacuum directions and output partitions.
Every regular chiral product and both convolution cuts remain. The recurrence is not a claim that the required primitives exist.

claims.statement: After unary normalization, two-output evaluation descends to the full global group \(H^2(K_1,D_0)\) and kills every global boundary. claims.statement: The twisted differential at the specified primitive-valued point retains scalar-output source operations, mixed vacuum inputs and every output action. A classification of all components of the exact zero-character fibre remains separate, including whether vanishing of the binary invariant characterizes the Koszul component. Other central-character fibres, the full central-restriction image and higher homotopy groups are not classified by these results. comparisons.title: Native marked fields on an intrinsic source
comparisons.overview: An actual completed source and noncritical marked evaluation are available. The stronger physical right-adjoint and operation comparisons have their own remaining conditions.

comparisons.title: State contractions, Ward classes and higher values
comparisons.overview: The noncritical state complex and relative Ward cohomology are explicit. Critical quadratic primitives exist in every algebraic weight; coherent critical and fixed-gauge higher choices remain distinct.

comparisons.title: Which completions preserve the native constructions?
comparisons.overview: The ordered, curved-bar and separated carriers have different domains. Explicit examples distinguish a valid finite prodiagram from an invalid ordinary-limit extension and isolate the uniformity required by Cartan transport and evaluation.

comparisons.title: Current carriers, contact quotients and coefficient size
comparisons.overview: Actual moment and relative-quotient comparisons are established on their finite native domains. Passing from polynomial coefficients to full analytic-functional coefficients, or adding a separated spectator, changes the relevant contact modules; the annular telescope supplies one precise full-coefficient comparison.

comparisons.title: Coupled residues and derived coalescence
comparisons.overview: Direct finite scalar coalescence, the derived two-branch diagonal and the first corrected three-copy association are constructed on actual current sources. The full relative and Koszul coordinates are essential, as are the finite jets of moving coefficients.

comparisons.title: Gaussian kernels and graph contact identities
comparisons.overview: Finite scalar Gaussian kernels and native sums are actual currents in a selected tame class. Every-pole triangle closure extends to a finite cycle and cactus contact tower. Nonzero four-cycle and diamond contacts show why this does not become a blanket closure statement for all graphs.

comparisons.title: Composition of admitted current images
comparisons.overview: Gaussian and finite top-normal contact outputs can be reused in disjoint-block compositions through their full actual kernels. This strict finite composition keeps the circuit relation, while its auxiliary differential and separated trace interface retain their own domains.

comparisons.title: From finite operations to the full physical comparison
comparisons.overview: Specified formal and restricted completions coexist with precise ordinary-distribution obstructions. The stronger physical comparison must retain the complete source relations, critical contacts and support conditions while extending the admitted inputs and height motions.

comparisons.title: One finite family and its actual native realization
comparisons.overview: One selected family carries exact unary maps, Cartan and translation compatibility, physical facets and units, the actual affine roof and the unchanged binary tensorator at every finite positive arity. Canonical ternary normalization gives contractible higher choices, and the polynomial continuous dual has an A∞ inverse. Fixed-base ternary, fixed-deletion and source-completion obstructions retain their stated domains.

comparisons.title: Finite Ward geometry with the signed full node
comparisons.overview: Absolute Ward chains admit a finite-top Chevalley model, and the normalized block has its actual KZ connection and all-degree right node action. Finite one-block sewing works over the specified common Laurent base with the signed left action. Infinite-test coefficient interchange, the positive Cartan-sign identification and literal removal of descendant poles fail in their stated forms.

comparisons.title: Scalar Wilson colimits and the actual current recipient
comparisons.overview: The current-defined recipient J_z realizes arbitrary unbounded scalar multiplicity complexes on a fixed finite Wilson pair and compares their colimit defects. Its isomorphism is detected on every original ambient smooth derived output test. Unrestricted smooth extraction has a separate nonzero defect comparison cone, and incoming higher maps lie beyond the scalar theorem.

comparisons.title: The regular relative dual and individual ghost lifts
comparisons.overview: The relative energywise dual and reversed-order coring retain the balanced line-algebra action on their stated perfect modules. A restricted continuous current model retains both incoming actions. Individual ghost morphism and element lifts can fail while the right ghost operator remains closed; unrestricted duals and full regular ambient geometry require different comparisons.

comparisons.title: Full output nodes and conditional ambient recognition
comparisons.overview: The homogeneous affine roof is a quasi-isomorphism of right node modules in every degree, and the representable node bar retains all word lengths. Its geometric extension requires an actual Ward resolution. A separate abstract criterion detects every ambient torsion test from a bounded-below representing object under explicit functorial hypotheses; neither result supplies arbitrary incoming higher-morphism compatibility.

comparisons.title: Interior tree sewing and genuine collision boundaries
comparisons.overview: Actual sewing is constructed on every finite binary interior tree, including all output-node degrees and compatible same-tree contraction orders. Distinct refinements use native associator transport. The finite interior theorem supplies the binary-tree conclusion beyond one-block sewing, while descendant poles obstruct literal restriction of unchanged algebraic chains at proper and root collision divisors.

comparisons.title: Real-height traces and full native endpoint fusion
comparisons.overview: One real height motion fuses a finite native cluster with its spectator through the singular sheet while retaining full currents and the first Ward transport.

comparisons.title: Physical incidence and the full first-circuit relative relation
comparisons.overview: The same motion has a proper point-contact incidence. It retains the chamber current and supplies the physical third branch needed by the complete first-circuit relation.

comparisons.title: Global endpoint categories and ordinary split descent
comparisons.overview: The full ordered collision atlas carries the polynomial/pro marked endpoint categories and their numerical all-matrix cut functors. Ordinary split descent has the exact integral semisimple charge criterion; completed geometric duality is a separate comparison.

comparisons.title: Native lattices and controlled formal duality
comparisons.overview: Finite-free native lattices now support a controlled quotient, an independent formal source, whole-word adjunction calculus and its absolute polar-pro extension. The literal support and pole order remains part of every mapping space.

comparisons.title: Smooth roots, colored cuts and coefficient bars
comparisons.overview: Full fixed-field smooth kernels admit rooted normal attachments, transported-color cut targets and a distinct ordinary-action single-root bar. Compatible cores give a fixed-configuration augmentation equivalence of coefficient complexes; full physical-actor linearity remains additional.

comparisons.title: Finite normal support and universal coefficients
comparisons.overview: The native all-pair support diagram has coherent finite-forest residues, normal transfer and admissible product-bar comparisons. Universal polar coefficients have their own finite-support pro comparison with a nonzero regular coefficient attachment; the entire original-Y row is not automatically identified with the pure-state support theorem.

comparisons.title: Laurent cap duality and native mates
comparisons.overview: A common Laurent bound and ordered finite cap support give an actual dual pair and continuous native full-bar mates in a fixed affine frame. The unchanged discrete Gaussian cap obstruction remains valid on its different carrier.

comparisons.title: Coherent coefficient maps for ordered caps

comparisons.title: Full base change in the centre construction

Arbitrary base arrows reduce to surjective ones, and objectwise coverage would supply the finite coherences. Universal coverage and the genuine actor comparison still require their own constructions.

comparisons.title: Which exterior-source mapping spaces are computed?
comparisons.overview: The full mapping space from one exterior generator is known in every odd integer degree. Finite families of degree-one generators have actual natural retracts; the extra factor for several generators remains to be determined.

comparisons.title: From bounded residue models to the ordinary tensor source

Exact interpolation would identify that fibration with the original tensor-source restriction in every homotopy degree. The original universal fixed-bound vanishing statement is false, while the distinct no-residue complex has all-charge amplitude.

comparisons.title: Binary primitives and coherent roots

comparisons.title: Supported induction and spectral operations
comparisons.overview: The native unit and kernel are explicit at every finite support. Their continuous duals carry an actual coherent tensorator for disjoint supports, while comparison with all ordinary acyclics and specialization to coincident supports remain separate.

comparisons.title: All-order moments and their native comparison
comparisons.overview: The actual trace source has finite positioned factors and compatible moments at every order. Actual normalization transports them, and one exact-matrix application fixes a precise full native prefix.

comparisons.title: Finite-order compatibility and the singleton choice

comparisons.title: The repaired native elliptic fields through sixth order

comparisons.title: The actual elliptic source and its completion

comparisons.title: From the selected source to the full native prefix
comparisons.overview: The source is matched to the complete fixed native fields through degree five and exchange through degree six. The finite sixth field exists independently; identifying that exact coefficient with the all-order extension remains the next comparison.

comparisons.title: Scalar twists and state-coordinate transport
comparisons.overview: Even and odd scalar jet operations have actual all-state meanings. Their exchange orientation and transported coactions control how a field normalization can be composed.

comparisons.title: Mixed coefficients and the common-category target
comparisons.overview: Actual mixed objects, generated supported maps and precisely marked rational and KZ instances are established. The full native category and an independent universal operation comparison retain their additional requirements.

comparisons.title: Completions, symbols and moment frames
comparisons.overview: Finite-stage Gaussian maps, completed symbolic tensors and changing-frame periods have explicit positive constructions. Their unrestricted completions, operator images and fixed-moment exchange comparisons have distinct scoped obstructions.

comparisons.title: Completed five-point sewing and vacuum units
comparisons.overview: The positive five-channel comparison, all vacuum placements and their fixed-source units are available on their completed domains. Mixed rational Ward covariance now holds on the exact nuclear graph tensor source.

comparisons.title: Fixed-input recipients and vacuum limits
comparisons.overview: Continuous rational Ward operations have explicit representing recipients for fixed point-module inputs. Point, meromorphic, graph-dual and joint logarithmic vacuum outputs retain their own topologies; the spectral cap has an exact source-regularity threshold.

comparisons.title: Which outputs can be sewn again?
comparisons.overview: Actual positive collisions are injective, and the source has exact projective tensor and quotient structure. Repeated sewing still needs its own input domain: proper annular and quotient sources work, while the whole common recipient fails the actual outer-seam test.

comparisons.title: Free elliptic reduction and its relative cubic comparison
comparisons.overview: The independent graph, polynomial-Thom histories and several actual singular normal families are constructed. The first augmented edge and two supported-prefix current limits retain their source terms and exact moments. Their full comparison with the original fixed current recipient and lower marking remains a stronger problem.

comparisons.title: Three-dimensional gravity and Liouville theory
comparisons.overview: The regulated stress theory has explicit ordinary and normal operations, source-algebra coherence and stronger finite-word limits. These results retain their actual source and recipient domains. A state prepared by independent Einstein-gravity amplitudes and the full physical operation comparison remain distinct targets.

comparisons.title: The native quantum stress and endpoint dictionary

The full quantum pushforward with stress and endpoint sources must still be compared with the independently prescribed target, including its physical parameter calibration and all required faces.

comparisons.title: Source-dependent caps and independently removed sewing cutoffs

The original-cycle convergence obstruction is compatible with the new contour result. The remaining physical cap comparison concerns the unnormalized scalar and phase, original coefficient-cutoff line, and a common source, heat and cut domain.

The theorem covers all complexes with torsion terms and identifies cohomological torsion when bounded below; the full unbounded recipient comparisons remain separate.

comparisons.title: Localization at the realization kernel

readingPaths.title: From the source to an actual field value
readingPaths.summary: Read the source definition and uniform bounds before the evaluation. Then inspect the retained values and the coefficient-restriction counterexample before turning to the stronger physical comparison.

stages.label: An intrinsic ordered rooted carrier
stages.description: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_3\), the ordered source \(N^{1-n}=\varprojlim_R\operatorname*{colim}_L(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}((G/J_L)^n,A)\otimes_{R_3,\mathrm{alg}}A_R)\) is a continuous dg bimodule over the full smooth native algebra \(A\). Both completed endpoint actions, translation and the scalar chain augmentation are defined. Finite expressions have a canonical dense map into this carrier.

stages.label: A global Cartan isomorphism with uniform Laurent bounds
stages.description: At every numerical \(K\) over \(R_3\), the restricted Laurent source has an actual continuous Cartan operator \(T=\lim_M T_M\). Its composition \(T^2\) defines strict inverse frame maps \(\Gamma^{\pm1}=1\pm\hbar T+\tfrac12\hbar^2T^2\). The resolved differential is the limit of the prescribed native rows and equals \(\Gamma d_{\rm ten}\Gamma^{-1}\). Both total and relative translation commute with the global frame map.

stages.label: Pure-root values extend to the ordered completion
stages.description: At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), the chosen finite pure-root evaluation extends uniquely and continuously to every rooted degree of the ordered carrier. The extension is a dg full-\(A\)-bimodule map, preserves both Ward laws and all prescribed scalar, first-root and native quadratic values, and retains the full algebraic trace factors. Its restricted Laurent version has finite coefficient convolution; the global source theorem supplies its chain and total-translation domain conditions.

stages.label: A marked evaluation on the completed ordered source
stages.description: At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), \(\mathcal E_{\rm ten}=\mathcal P+\mathcal J+\Xi\), with \(\Xi=d_Q\mathcal H+\mathcal H d_{\rm ten}\), is an actual continuous dg bimodule evaluation for the full smooth native algebra. It is defined on every homogeneous element of the ordered polynomial marked carrier and its specified restricted Laurent extension. It has both coefficient-indexed Ward laws and transports through the finite and global Cartan isomorphisms.

stages.label: The evaluation keeps the field and its fixed normalizations
stages.description: For the checked noncritical \(R_3\) marked evaluation, the scalar value is the whole field, and every prescribed first-root homotopy and the full native \(q_\hbar\) column survive. The classical oriented \(H[1]\wedge H[-1]\) value on \(q\) is \(4/u\). Positive inserted cycles take \(q_\hbar\) to \(-\mathrm{id}\) and \(\omega_\hbar\) to \(+\mathrm{id}\). The inserted Casimir and first mixed values retain their prescribed native terms and trace phases.

stages.label: Literal coefficient restriction does not give the evaluation
stages.description: The direct marked evaluation differs from \(\epsilon_C\alpha_{\rm tr}\). For the signed trace root \(r_{I,0}^{\rm Ch}=-r_{c^I_{-1}}^{\rm raw}\) with unit endpoints, their values on the same finite-frame source and trace-ghost test are \(-\mathrm{id}\) and zero. A raw singleton would give \(+\mathrm{id}\), so the sign convention matters. Agreement on scalar and ghost-free trace-current states does not supply a factorization.

stages.label: The stronger physical and operation comparison
stages.description: The remaining physical target is to identify the checked carrier and evaluation with the prescribed full marked right adjoint, impose its full \(R_2\) and unit-relative normalization, and compare native ordered products, supported residues, collisions and tensorators on the required domains. Full right-dual and merged-mode completion, coefficient biduality, completed bar/cobar comparison and compatible higher precision require separate constructions.

readingPaths.title: From state obstructions to the limits of completion
readingPaths.summary: Begin with the state retract and the relative Ward tests. Compare the all-level canonical residual and critical quadratic result, then examine why a finite coefficient diagram need not admit an ordinary-limit value.

stages.label: The noncritical native state complex has a small retract
stages.description: At each fixed numerical \(K\ne-2\) over \(R_3\), the actual states \(1,q_\hbar,\omega_\hbar\), with \(dq_\hbar=2T\omega_\hbar\), sit in a translation-linear strong deformation retract retaining all trace-current polynomials and trace ghosts. Ordinary state cohomology is \((R_3\mathbf1\oplus R_3[\omega_\hbar])\otimes L\), with no extra \(\hbar\)-torsion. Precomposition gives the corresponding shifted-Hom dg bimodule retract.

stages.label: Relative Ward cohomology retains the full trace factor
stages.description: At fixed \(K\ne-2\), let \(\mathcal Z_p=\ker(\partial_u-(-)T_L)\) on \(\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(L^p,\mathcal E)\), with \(\mathcal Z_p=0\) for \(p<0\) and \(\mathcal E=\operatorname{Hom}_{R_3}(V,V((u)))\). Then \(H^m(Q_{\rm rel})\cong\mathcal Z_{1-m}\oplus\mathcal Z_{-2-m}\oplus\delta_{m,-1}\mathcal E_{\rm const}\). Only the scalar trace state contributes the separate \(q_\hbar\)-residue obstruction.

stages.label: A conditional test for relative Ward primitives
stages.description: An already defined closed relative-Ward forcing of degree \(-1\) has a relative-Ward primitive precisely when its value on \(1\otimes L^2\) and its scalar-trace residue on \(q_\hbar\otimes1\) vanish. In degree \(-2\), the tests are its values on \(1\otimes L^3\) and \(\omega_\hbar\otimes L^0\); there is no additional residue test on every trace state. Ordinary exactness is weaker: the difference between the prescribed classical \(4/u\) quadratic value and the contraction primitive has residue \(4\,\mathrm{id}\) and is not a relative-Ward boundary.

stages.label: The coupled canonical quadratic/cubic residual is solved
stages.description: The native operators satisfy \(\mathscr D Z_q=2\partial_u Z_\omega\) and \(\mathscr D Z_\omega=0\). The coupled fixed-frame residual equations have explicit solutions at every numerical level, including zero and critical level, on the declared finite-composition domain and its separating smooth structural coefficient hull. The source gauges retain the prescribed first term and the mixed second-order term with coefficient one; both Ward laws and strict rooted units hold.

stages.label: Critical quadratic primitives exist at all algebraic weights
stages.description: At \(K=-2\), every actual signed quadratic pure-root forcing with the prescribed first homotopies annihilates every algebraic native degree-one cycle. It therefore has an individual ordinary \(R_3\)-linear primitive with the stated pointwise Laurent bound, in every algebraic weight. The all-weight classical generation theorem and the full trace factor are included.

stages.label: Finite projected coefficients form a valid prodiagram
stages.description: For every numerical \(K\) over \(R_3\), the normalized finite free closed complexes with basis \(u^te j_t\), \(0\le t<T\), have actual images \(u^t(1\otimes X_H(-t-1))e\) in the checked carrier. The projections commute with right-quotient transitions and truncation of the nonnegative Laurent coefficients below exponent \(T\).

stages.label: The ordinary inverse limit exceeds finite right support
stages.description: The finite projection has no coefficient-preserving ordinary-inverse-limit value in the checked global carrier. Its required series has infinitely many independent right PBW coordinates already at the first right quotient modulo \(\hbar\), while that carrier requires finite right support across the whole series. The witness has fixed word length, degree and conformal weight, Laurent floor zero and a common scalar middle cutoff. Its scalar-vacuum state series is nevertheless a legitimate Laurent series.

stages.label: A common ghost cutoff is necessary for these extensions
stages.description: Coefficientwise membership in the ordered source is insufficient for its Laurent extension. If the ghost cutoff may grow with the exponent, the explicit Cartan example has a retained coefficient proportional to \(M-1\), and the pure trace-root example has evaluation coefficient \(-(M+1)u^{-1}\). Allowing a separate Laurent pole bound at each ghost coordinate also defeats the pure contraction. These arrays lie outside the checked uniform domain.

readingPaths.title: From a computed source to the genuine action question
readingPaths.summary: An editorial route through the distinctions between a complete source calculation, detected multigenerator factors and the separate genuine Heisenberg comparison.

stages.label: The complete one-generator source space and the actual polynomial map
stages.description: For every ordinary algebraic, possibly unbounded dg vertex target \(B\), the degree-one exterior source satisfies \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(\Lambda(\epsilon),B)\simeq Z^1((B\otimes\Omega_\bullet)^{hT})\). Its components are \(H^1(B^{hT})\), and its based \(n\)-th homotopy group is \(H^{1-n}(B^{hT})\). The previously constructed polynomial map \(\nu\) is itself an equivalence for target \(\Lambda(\epsilon)\), giving \(\mathbb C^2_{\rm disc}\times K(\mathbb C,1)\). Its original composition law is retained: \((\lambda,\beta,\omega)\star(\lambda',\beta',\omega')=(\lambda\lambda',\lambda'\beta+\beta',\lambda'\omega+\omega')\), with the rightmost map applied first. The conditional quartet comparison and the vanishing scalar singular-product detector retain their stated scopes. The source calculation does not identify the genuine Heisenberg actor map \(q_B\).

stages.label: One exterior generator is computed in every odd degree
stages.description: Let \(d\) be any odd integer, including a negative one, and let \(\Lambda(\epsilon_d)\) have \(|\epsilon_d|=d\) and \(d\epsilon_d=T\epsilon_d=0\). For every ordinary algebraic dg vertex algebra \(B\), unbounded in either direction if desired, \[\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(\Lambda(\epsilon_d),B)\simeq Z^d(B^{hT}\otimes\Omega_\bullet).\] Hence \(\pi_0=H^d(B^{hT})\) and \(\pi_n=H^{d-n}(B^{hT})\) at every basepoint. Here \((B^{hT})^j=B^j\oplus B^{j-1}\), with differential \((\partial b,Tb-\partial b')\). No connectivity, commutativity or target arity grading is assumed.

stages.label: Finite exterior sources have detected components and loops
stages.description: For \(A_r=\Lambda(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_r)\), finite \(r\ge1\), all generators in degree one with \(d=T=0\), let \(B\) be a commutative dg vertex algebra strictly concentrated in nonnegative degrees. Put \(M_B=Z^1((B\otimes\Omega_\bullet)^{hT})\) and \(H_B=Z^0(B)\cap\ker T\). The actual map \[M_B^r\times(H_B)_{\rm disc}^{\binom r2}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(A_r,B)\] has a natural homotopy left inverse. For \(B=\mathbb C\), its detected components are \(V^*\oplus\Lambda^2V^*\) and loops are \(V^*\), where \(V\) is spanned by the exterior generators. Alternation and basis changes agree with those invariants. The theorem gives a retract, not exhaustion of the full mapping space.

stages.label: Two generators split off an additive scalar factor
stages.description: The derived enveloping adjunction identifies the scalar mapping space from two degree-one exterior generators with its full dg Lie conformal mapping space. The detected \(\mathbb C^3_{\rm disc}\times K(\mathbb C^2,1)\) factor splits additively, giving a product with the homotopy fibre over zero of the actual retraction. That complementary factor is uncomputed. The positive-arity conformal cochain calculation is valid as a calculation, but no equivalence from it to all derived roofs has been proved.

stages.label: Every genuine loop detector has scalar image
stages.description: At every point \(\alpha\) of the genuine unit fibre \(\mathscr F_A(B)\), with its specified unit homotopy retained, the state-complex loop detector has exactly \(\operatorname{im}\chi_\alpha=\mathbb C\,\mathrm{id}_{U(A)}\). The actual loops \(\epsilon\mapsto\epsilon+\mu\,ds\) give an additive central section, compatible with basepoint transport, and an isomorphism of groups \[\pi_1(\mathscr F_A(B),\alpha)\cong\mathbb C_{\mathrm{add}}\times\ker\chi_\alpha.\] The kernel is not proved abelian or zero. At the displayed \(q_B\) points, this scalar factor already comes from the source. On a chosen component, the scalar-detector fibre \(\Phi_\alpha\) is connected, with \(\pi_1(\Phi_\alpha)=\ker\chi_\alpha\) and \(\pi_n(\Phi_\alpha)=\pi_n(\mathscr F_A(B),\alpha)\) for \(n\ge2\); these groups and contractibility remain open. Strict sphere roofs retain their comparison paths: forgetting those paths gives free-sphere orbits, conjugacy classes in degree one. If the required primitive map extends after refinement to an \(f^{\prime}\)-derivation \(E\) with \(Ed=D\), the sufficient pointed nullhomotopy is \[G=f^{\prime}+\theta_n(1-s)D-ds\,\theta_nE.\] The negative final term is necessary in even degree as well. The proved binary vanishing is \(E_0(x_{1(m)}x_2)=0\) for closed degree-one inputs on every kernel-loop roof, for all \(m\). It does not cover arbitrary binary relations with nonclosed inputs or prove that \(E\) exists. The full source-image comparison, completeness of \((\operatorname{ch},\operatorname{ct})\), \(q_B\), base transitions and \(\lambda_B\) remain open.

stages.label: Full base change and the genuine centre comparison
stages.description: For the nonzero-level Heisenberg algebra \(A\), determine whether the required base transitions of the full two-legged cocycle categories induce nerve weak equivalences, with every original source refinement and admissible target link retained. Every base arrow now reduces to a surjective factor. Universal incoming tame coverage for those surjective transitions remains the exact missing condition: the full ideal generated by the image of the base kernel must be acyclic. The genuine actor comparison \(q_B\), with its specified unit homotopy, remains separate, as do the full nilpotent inclusion and the strict-coslice to infinity-undercategory comparison.

readingPaths.title: Why finite bounds and exact interpolation must be separated
readingPaths.summary: An editorial route from the exact low-charge results through the fixed-bound counterexample and the different no-residue theorem, then to the actual conditional tensor-source comparison.

stages.label: Matched residue complexes are exact in the proved ranges
stages.description: For the algebraic residue complex \(D(r;q)\) with its prescribed matched finite bounds, whole polynomial spectator base and positive odd \(\mu\), restricted correlation duality and the normalized de Rham-plus-left-residue differential hold. Charge two is acyclic for every number of spectators; one spectator is exact in every charge at least two; charge one retains only its spectator coefficient module. At the matched one-step bounds, \(H^0(D)=H^1(D)=0\) for charges at least two. Repeated colours require finite stabilizer invariants, and the state degree is \(\sum_j|c_j|+q-n\). The separate cellular top-two theorem retains its charge and arity qualifications.

stages.label: Two spectators already defeat universal fixed-bound exactness
stages.description: In the literal matched complex, take \(r=2\), \(q=4\), \(N_{12}=0\), \(b_1=b_2=1\) and \(\mu=1\). The displayed rational cocycle gives \(H^4(D(2;4))\ne0\) at homogeneity \(-15\). Because \(n=q=4\), the proposed universal vanishing for \(n\le q\) is false for these unchanged bounds. The example is compatible with the proved low-charge and one-spectator ranges. It gives no general obstruction to enlarged bounds, cofinal systems, nonzero cellular differentials or the full centre comparison.

stages.label: Without residue cells, all charges have a two-degree amplitude
stages.description: Let \(A(r;q)\) be the sign-anti-invariant rational relative form complex with horizontal differential only, no residue cells and the original finite coefficientwise pole bounds. For all finite spectator and charge numbers, every allowed bound and positive odd \(\mu\), \(H^i(A(r;q))=0\) for \(i<q-1\). Thus only form degrees \(q-1,q\) can occur when \(q\ge1\); at charge zero only degree zero occurs. The theorem holds over the whole polynomial spectator base, including collisions. The normalized extraction \(F=EJE\) gives a primitive summand with cohomology only in degree \(q\). Raw \(E^2=0\) is false.

stages.label: Nonzero differentials can be adapted to matched locality bounds
stages.description: The cellular adaptation constructs a surjective state quasi-isomorphism with nonzero source differential, actual evaluation domination and the literal all-state relations, including \(h(d_Tc)\). The accepted charge-zero, charge-one and charge-two conclusions transfer on that construction, and the stated finite-charge exact quotients are actual dg vertex quotients. An arbitrary evaluation need not annihilate the discarded higher-charge ideal. This gives genuine low-charge progress while leaving universal all-charge exact interpolation separate.

stages.label: Directed lifting gives the full mapping-space comparison
stages.description: For a small directed inverse system \(Q_i\), suppose every lifting problem against a surjective state quasi-isomorphism lifts after a later transition. Then \(\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(Q_i,B\otimes\Omega_\bullet)\) is Kan and naturally equivalent to \(\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Q_i,B)\), without a simplicity assumption. Every object has an honest directed system of trivial fibrations with this property. For a specified augmentation to \(X\), identifying this space with \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(X,B)\) still requires the actual exact-interpolation factorizations through quasi-isomorphic objects over \(X\).

stages.label: Exact interpolation gives the full tensor-source fibre theorem
stages.description: Suppose that, for every stage of the actual system \(S_W\), a later transition factors over \(W\otimes\Lambda(\epsilon)\) through an actual state quasi-isomorphism \(Y\to W\otimes\Lambda(\epsilon)\). Then the universal fibration is equivalent, as an arrow of spaces, to \[\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(W\otimes\Lambda(\epsilon),B)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(\Lambda(\epsilon),B).\] Its homotopy fibre over \(\phi\) is \(\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(W,B^{h\delta_\phi})\) in every homotopy degree. The tensor product here is ordinary. Universal evaluation-compatible exact interpolation remains unproved.

stages.label: The remaining route must preserve evaluation through all charges
stages.description: The fixed matched-bound claim of nonnegative exactness has a counterexample; that universal claim is no longer an open target. The constructive questions concern suitably changed or cofinal models and their actual transition maps, a verified all-charge evaluation-compatible exact-interpolation property for the ordinary tensor source, and convergence for nonclosed attachments or completed recipients. No-residue amplitude and low-charge adaptation supply inputs to this route without proving its full-residue or pro consumers.

readingPaths.summary: An editorial route through the two different kinds of relative comparison: the action’s full pointing and the marked cut’s full normal recipient.

stages.label: Separate the two fibres
stages.description: The singleton higher class and the noncontractible binary filler torsor concern their stated restriction problems. The vacuum-evaluation recipient supplies the recognition criterion.

stages.label: Retain the unary path
stages.description: Unrestricted translation leaves a precise unary defect in the normal identity. The path correction removes that defect under full-layer hypotheses, which the canonical chiral integration verifies.

stages.label: Retain both relative components
stages.description: Partial deletion and the two-vacuum comparison keep the specified open paths and permitted collisions. Their conclusions do not fill the remaining marked relative class.

stages.label: Read the conditional descent exactly
stages.description: The full pointed recipient identifies the detector image to kill. Full kernel maps would give the overlap path used by two-label descent; the generic linear test is not an actor counterexample.

readingPaths.title: From corrected induction to continuous duals
readingPaths.summary: Read the full algebraic equivalence and its weak class, then compare the marked, completed and reflected realizations before their continuous spectral operations. This is an editorial route, not an extra dependency theorem.

stages.label: Corrected induction on the full unbounded category
stages.description: Corrected induction gives an enhanced equivalence K_sm(Y)[W_F^−1] ≃ D(Sm_μ), with actual restricted twisted coinduction as inverse. Its unit, counit and triangles preserve the universal-vacuum mark and ordinary composition.

stages.label: Ordinary quasi-isomorphisms are too broad for algebraic induction
stages.description: On the full algebraic smooth source, W_F is strictly smaller than the ordinary quasi-isomorphisms at every level. A root-localized smooth affine module gives an ordinary acyclic coefficient complex whose induction is nonzero.

stages.label: The marked comparison in every energy
stages.description: There is an actual energy-preserving dg isomorphism E_W† ≅ G_μ(D_σV_μ(W)). Its counit composite P_W:F_μ(E_W†)→D_σV_μ(W) is an affine chain quasi-isomorphism in every energy and carries F_μ(q_W†) strictly to the normalized contravariant-form map, naturally in W.

stages.label: Induction on the complete energy category
stages.description: On the one-sided subquadratic support category, the actual completed unit and counit are continuous vector-complex deformation equivalences. The strict continuous adjunction gives an enhanced equivalence from the F̂-detected localization to the ordinary quasi-isomorphism localization of the complete affine recipient, preserving the completed vacuum and composition.

stages.label: A critical obstruction in the completed category
stages.description: At every simple-g critical level μ=−h, an ordinary acyclic complete affine complex M has nonzero completed coinduction: ĜM continuously retracts as a vector complex onto the completed exterior algebra on degree-one generators ξ_r with zero differential. Thus Ĝ does not preserve all ordinary quasi-isomorphisms and Qis⊊W_F̂.

stages.label: Exactly when reflected cochains preserve ordinary equivalences
stages.description: The reflected null class equals all ordinary acyclics precisely outside M={1−6(p−q)²/(pq): p,q≥2, gcd(p,q)=1}. At those line charges, the same functors give D(Y_c)≃D(N_(26−c)) for every unbounded complex.

stages.label: The exact exceptional charge locus
stages.description: For every c=1−6(p−q)²/(pq) with coprime p,q≥2, the reflected null class is strictly smaller than ordinary acyclicity, and Φ is nonconservative. A specified ordinary-acyclic contragredient-Verma telescope has a surviving class in H^−1Ψ.

stages.label: Actual opposition between induction and coinduction
stages.description: At complementary charges κ=26−c, the balanced pairing identifies completed native induction with the full weak dual of restricted reflected coinduction on every discrete coefficient. In the opposite direction, full continuous reflected coinduction is the full weak dual of ordinary native induction on every native smooth input, including the signed unit and counit.

stages.label: The actual continuous spectral tensorator
stages.description: The separated-support spectral operator converges on the full completed tensor. Full right coinduction and product-exterior cochains have actual signed adjunction maps, and the dual native induction tensorator is a chain homeomorphism with every finite-arity coherence identity. The products descend through the specified detected weak class.

readingPaths.title: From actual fields to the remaining native comparison
readingPaths.summary: Begin with the actual trace source, compare its all-order native realization with the finite sixth-field theorem, then follow the moment and mixed-category comparisons. The reading order is editorial; only the displayed checked edges assert mathematical relations.

stages.label: An actual elliptic field algebra at every order
stages.description: The selected determinant-free RTT algebra has actual local formal quantum vertex operations at every hbar order. At critical offset beta=hbar, its ordinary trace generates a closed field ideal J, and the split quotient B/J is P[[hbar]]. Fields, exchange, translation, vacuum and period operations descend to this actual quotient.

stages.label: The full native quintic prefix has an all-order realization
stages.description: An actual all-order quantum vertex algebra on P[[hbar]] agrees with the complete fixed native fields Y0 through Y5 and exchange S0 through S6 on every polynomial state, with independent input jets and every output coefficient. Its exact identities include both hexagons, weak associativity, unitarity, Yang–Baxter and spectator-independent locality at each precision.

stages.label: A complete sixth field on the fixed native prefix
stages.description: The repaired native elliptic fields extend to an actual local formal quantum vertex algebra on P⊗C[ℏ]/(ℏ⁷). The construction supplies the full sixth field on every algebraic polynomial state, with creation, translation, weak associativity, exchange locality and both complete sixth field hexagons.

stages.label: The remaining sixth-field comparison is precise
stages.description: A complete chosen sixth field already exists in the finite native theory modulo hbar⁷. The separate all-order realization matches its fields through degree five and its exchange through degree six. Equality of its sixth field with that chosen finite Y6, and hence equality of the whole finite structure, remains an additional comparison.

stages.label: The actual trace source has moments to every order
stages.description: The factors F_I give commuting actions mu_r(a)=a(lambda) and mu_l(a)=F_I^−1 a(lambda−hbar H_I)F_I. Actual partial fusions and exchanges intertwine these actions to every order; the raw source singleton is H.

stages.label: An exact-matrix realization has all-order moments
stages.description: The actual exact-matrix quantum vertex algebra has compatible two-base moments at every deformation order. Its checked native comparison identifies the complete fields through degree three, the complete exchange through degree four, and the generating exchange matrix on all independent linear jets to every order.

stages.label: A higher native prefix needs its own moment application
stages.description: The exact-matrix moment application fixes full native fields through degree three and full exchange through degree four. A comparison with separately normalized higher native coefficients is an additional moment application, even when those fields and exchanges exist independently.

stages.label: Generated supported operations have continuous domains
stages.description: The explicit generated mixed supported maps extend continuously through every fixed finite forest on bounded current/jet stages with finite non-Gaussian state spans. Their three collision routes come from one fixed-three-diagonal common germ and satisfy L−R+N=0, with the stated finite numerator bound.

stages.label: The neutral rational instance includes all its horizontal maps
stages.description: An algebraic rational QVA with the supplied statewise finite Laurent exchange embeds into the mixed construction with its state, coefficient and field maps, supported residues, finite normals, all three collision channels and units. Every horizontal map between neutral diagrams has its contextual lift beside nonneutral spectators. Consecutive cuts give structural equality; other separated-group cuts retain their signed exchange arrows.

stages.label: The marked sl2 KZ instance retains its actual arrows
stages.description: For kappa=k+2 outside the rational numbers, the supplied generated sl2 KZ/Ward coefficient category embeds with its states, connection, evaluations, cuts and three supported channels. The normalized Gamma marking, half-braiding and translated hbar/2 test are preserved. Coordinate inverse transport and row-symbol transposition remain distinct operations.

stages.label: The full common-category comparison remains stronger
stages.description: The local elliptic field theorems and the typed rational, KZ and Gaussian instances still need the full common native comparison with genuine mixed tensors, independently defined colour-operation spaces, their multiplicative Ward map and the prescribed supported cut and unit maps. Selected integral lattices, global field-period comparison, recognition and analytic or physical sewing are further specified comparisons.

readingPaths.title: From a sewn map to an admissible next input
readingPaths.summary: Start with the completed five-channel and mixed Ward maps, then examine their representing recipients. Finish with source separation, injectivity and the outer-seam restriction to see why a continuous output still needs a specified source for the next operation. This is an editorial route, not a claim that every step is a mathematical dependency.

stages.label: Five channels on the full ordered interior
stages.description: The five independently sewn positive-input channel germs have compatible completed continuations over the logarithmic bidisc 0<|x|,|y|<1, with z1=xy and z2=y, and hence over 0<z1<z2<1. Four entire-energy inputs are admitted, with one sufficient finite Hilbert source stage on each compact configuration set and one fixed regularized output. Both internal spectra, the output spectrum and all descendant levels remain uncut. The extreme nested tree has raw inverse-Gram convergence on this bidisc; the other four retain their own raw sewing domains.

stages.label: Every placement of one vacuum input
stages.description: The canonical mixed sewings, their middle and endpoint constructions, and their reflected comparisons cover all four positions of one vacuum input. They admit full entangled sources, retain all levels and spectra, and satisfy the coefficient-one unit triangles on the admitted stages. The outer vacuum field takes the sharp three-positive-input output into a fixed strictly negative energy stage. The left unit includes its coordinate translation, and every channel keeps its own two-binary normalization.

stages.label: Full rational Ward identities for the mixed maps
stages.description: Every rational vector field with poles at the four inputs and infinity acts on the complete mixed graph source, and the actual sewn maps satisfy its Ward identity in one fixed negative-energy output space. This includes arbitrary entangled inputs and the normally convergent local germ series. All four vacuum placements have these identities throughout the real ordered interior and on local complex neighbourhoods.

stages.label: A common representing recipient for fixed inputs
stages.description: For two fixed positive point-module inputs, the closed common carrier represents the declared full rational Ward operations into the Gaussian-growth section recipient, positive spectral strong duals, the meromorphic recipient, the vacuum graph dual, and closed invariant subspaces of arbitrary products of these targets. The morphisms are ordinary continuous Virasoro intertwiners. The common carriers themselves are admitted targets, and actual energy dilations use the same carrier at every nonzero logarithmic coordinate.

stages.label: The vacuum graph is nuclear
stages.description: The original mode-stable vacuum graph is nuclear. Adjoining the raising word L_-2 D to a finite set of graph words gives trace-class maps between the actual Hilbert graph completions, and a cofinal increasing system of such norms retains exactly the original topology.

stages.label: The full mixed array source is a projective tensor
stages.description: The actual fourfold graph-array space is canonically G completed-projective-tensor E_A completed-projective-tensor E_B completed-projective-tensor E_C. Every entangled array is included. It is nuclear, and each array has a decomposable series absolutely convergent in every projective seminorm. The binary positive entire-energy source likewise equals its full coefficient-array Hilbert intersection.

stages.label: Separate input actions are controlled on the source
stages.description: On the completed projective tensor of two positive entire-energy modules, finite polynomial vector fields approximate each separate regular input mode with geometric error after one source-seminorm strengthening. Every closed linear subspace invariant under the joint regular action therefore inherits the separate regular actions.

stages.label: Regular covariance detects the whole completed source
stages.description: A continuous linear map from the positive entire-energy tensor source to a Hausdorff locally convex target is injective if it intertwines all regular joint modes and has nonzero highest-input image. Separate source energy projections detect a nonzero finite-bidegree component, and the regular input actions then detect the highest tensor. Linearity is necessary for this criterion.

stages.label: Actual positive collisions lose no source vector
stages.description: The actual common, Gaussian, meromorphic, fixed-positive-point and strict integrated collisions are injective on the positive entire-energy tensor source under their construction hypotheses. Any nonempty open positive spectral interval still detects the entire input. The equal-label graph-dual vacuum operation is injective as well. These are injectivity conclusions, without an inverse or an identification of source and recipient-induced topologies.

stages.label: Proper annular sources support actual finite sewing
stages.description: For a fixed Gaussian Banach source stage, sufficiently long annular preparation gives actual canonical sewing on full entangled fields, with absolutely convergent spectral integrals and descendant contractions. The bare preparation threshold is strict; a collision kernel with its own Gaussian decay can include its endpoint. Finite chains admit compatible energy margins, and one annulus can be chosen uniformly on each bounded source subset. These source-dependent statements retain the propagated, scaled input modes.

stages.label: The actual common output cannot be the whole next input
stages.description: The actual fixed-output outer primary sewing cannot extend continuously to every vector of the common recipient, even after any one fixed finite incoming annulus. Its forced scalar negative-mode coefficients grow linearly at the outer puncture, whereas the common recipient has a convergent negative-mode series there. The actual complete cluster quotient source still carries the sewing continuously and maps densely into the recipient with its finer topology.

stages.label: The remaining comparison is an input-source category
stages.description: The stronger objective is a compatible test-source assignment for arbitrary recipient objects, actual binary operations on those sources, stability under repeated sewing, and identification of the associator and unit maps with the sewn maps. Fixed-input representability, all-placement fixed-source unit triangles, mixed rational Ward covariance and the nuclear tensor-source structure are available. Their coexistence does not supply the arbitrary-object construction.

readingPaths.title: Keep the current before taking its trace
readingPaths.summary: Begin with the independent graph and the sixteen polynomial-Thom histories. Compare the actual transverse and supported families, follow their signed fourth moments, and then inspect the augmented-edge source term and the remaining fixed-recipient comparison. This editorial route keeps current limits, trace identities and relative homotopies distinct.

stages.label: Incoming relations and an independent graph realization
stages.description: For the chosen labelled cubic matching with two occurrences of root U and one of root V, the incoming relation cylinder descends to the actual current image with its full source differential. The independent graph-current and central-bar realization has actual Wick operations and a square-zero differential before trace. The fixed-branch polynomial-to-supported normal comparison supplies its ordered cubic source inverse; these constructions retain the individual branches and central outputs.

stages.label: All sixteen histories on the polynomial-Thom carrier
stages.description: Complete root-and-central collar matrices construct all sixteen cubic histories on the specified polynomial-Thom graph-first carrier. The resulting untraced transferred operation has its own source chain equation. Finite prisms for all subsets of the six scalar contact coordinates retain their face identities, normal connections, support and excess factors. Scalar repeated-root vanishing holds on its stated exterior-degree-zero domain.

stages.label: Actual first-order source and contact prisms
stages.description: On the evaluated graph-marked scalar root and finite-jet domain, the native first residue equals its independent counterpart. The first-order source comparison and its full cone retain both source rows and the localization and coordinate endpoint terms. The specified first-contact primitive and radial lower-section regularizations have actual open, proper-pair and point current limits.

stages.label: A nonzero fourth-order current can have zero trace
stages.description: The original one-field normal collar has controlled current limits on the anchored three-covariance word. Its displayed bare compact-partner alpha kernel has a strictly positive fourth moment and an untraced point current of exact order four, with coefficient M/2, although its proper central-base trace is zero. Weighted Green-leg alpha terms retain a nonzero commutator correction; their vanishing cannot be inferred from the unweighted case.

stages.label: The first transverse normal family is realized
stages.description: Finite q-smooth strong-current families admit the actual finite normal relation projection, compatible with the full differential and both normal Weyl actions. On the first ordered transverse family u_v tensor v_w, every exterior row, finite jet and q-independent branch face satisfies the normalized canonical-current comparison.

stages.label: One supported field has its own current limit
stages.description: Replacing one field by its signed supported section, with its matching unweighted radial primitive and four remaining top Thom fields, gives the stated limits in all three pair positions. The eta and s limits and the g rows vanish, while the c_t alpha point order is at most 4+J+q. The displayed bare supported-prefix moment obeys M_sp>M_sm>0, has coefficient M_sp/2 and exact order four, and retains zero proper central trace at its declared coefficient scope.

stages.label: The singular supported partner is realized at fresh degree zero
stages.description: The canonical supported-partner projection is an actual current map in all four exterior rows when the fresh incoming normal variable has degree zero. It retains every finite old-root, graph-slot and primitive-slot jet, the full boundary and the central, root and frame squares. Its zero-jet matrix is nonzero, and the first-root Taylor correction contains both 1/3 and -1/6.

stages.label: One fully supported earlier pair is an actual single action
stages.description: For the ordered word a1 a2 u3 v4 v5 v6, the fully supported earlier pair factors through the prescribed single root action on the independent (U,t) coefficient domain. The eta and s limits and g rows vanish, and the c_t alpha point order is at most 4+J+q. The exhibited bare fourth moment is strictly negative, with coefficient M/2 and exact order four; its proper central-base trace vanishes on the stated restricted coefficient domain.

stages.label: A nonzero first augmented edge agrees in the prescribed order
stages.description: The actual first augmented section edge is constructed with all designated raw pair jets, the complete central Taylor correction, its normal primitive and both prism vertex legs. Native and independent section edges agree and are nonzero when the order and contraction agree. Reversing the order retains an intersection projector and a source term; those terms cannot be discarded before identifying the fixed lower comparison.

stages.label: The remaining native comparison has explicit inputs
stages.description: The supported-partner formula becomes the original native operation only after the full original-current-to-fixed-normal comparison is supplied, including tangent contraction, inverse, determinant factors and unchanged lower cochains. The root-plus-central native unit and basis matrix must also be identified; in the prescribed pure scalar normalization its factor kappa must equal one. At quadratic order, the independent source comparison additionally requires an actual primitive for the displayed residue discrepancy.

stages.label: The full relative cubic homotopy remains to be constructed
stages.description: The full relative cubic comparison must act on the original fixed current recipient, preserve the prescribed lower coefficients, and include the complete generated history words, branch and incidence maps, localization rows, compact endpoint and fixed lower marking. The actual normal-family, first-edge and supported-prefix results supply specific parts of that comparison. A nonzero untraced current with zero proper trace is not yet a correction-invariant obstruction to the complete homotopy.

readingPaths.title: From a Gaussian formula to a prepared cap
readingPaths.summary: An editorial route separating a finite integral, a normalized limit and the unnormalized physical state.

stages.label: Keep the full finite integral
stages.description: Start with the sourced finite Gaussian and evaluated collar, retaining covariance, semidensity and the raw scalar.

stages.label: Compare the available limits
stages.description: Read the common relative heat theorem and the normalized corner state together with the new contour construction and the original-cycle obstruction.

stages.label: Recover the physical line
stages.description: Finite zero- and nonzero-frequency sewing determine specific line maps. The final comparison must also determine the original physical normalization and phase.

readingPaths.title: Which analytic domain supports the comparison?
readingPaths.summary: An editorial route through the distinct ordinary, original Hodge and changed-carrier statements.

stages.label: Ordinary smooth inputs
stages.description: The ordinary reduced inverse and completed formal observable Gaussian specify their own source neighborhood, grading and topology.

stages.label: The boundary changes the Hodge question
stages.description: Compare the zero-boundary heat theorem with the obstruction for nonzero boundary sources on the original graph closure.

stages.label: A new carrier has its own comparison task
stages.description: The local cyclic gauge has compact heat on its declared paired carriers. The physical insertion and cap comparisons must identify the required domains and line data.

readingPaths.title: Follow the ordinary source unit
readingPaths.summary: Read the critical witness together with its native hypotheses, then the full unit model and the source localization. Finish with the remaining local-unit comparison. This is an editorial order, not a mathematical dependency chain.

stages.label: A perfect source for the universal vacuum
stages.description: At critical level, E=Y₀⊗ᴸ_{U(g)}C is perfect and has cohomology in nonnegative internal weights. Under the native comparison hypotheses, its actual realization is the universal vacuum V, and V belongs to thick(W). The actual supported unit lifts the homogeneous vacuum extensions to E and preserves their finite products.

stages.label: The ordinary global unit fails at critical level
stages.description: For every nonzero simple complex g at affine level μ=−h, put E=Y₀⊗ᴸ_{U(g)}C. The ordinary algebraic telescope L=hocolim_(r≥0) E[r]⟨−r(r+3)/2⟩, using the lifted quadratic-jet extensions, is nonzero and has Φ(L)=0. Its actual unit is L→0 with nonzero cone L[1]. This holds graded and ungraded under the stated native hypotheses.

stages.label: Compactness fails inside the generated recipient
stages.description: At the same critical levels, X=⊕_(r≥0)V[r]⟨−r(r+3)/2⟩ admits the actual map (1−σ)⁻¹j₀:V→X with a nonzero projection to every summand, where σ sends each summand to the next by its shifted vacuum extension and j₀ includes the first summand. Thus V and W are not compact inside Loc(W) ungraded, and inside the category generated by every energy shift of W when graded.

stages.label: A model of the actual unit on every ordinary input
stages.description: Under the native hypotheses, a strict smooth right-R model Q representing W with its supplied marked native action, a semifree resolution F→L, and a genuine smooth K-injective replacement j:Q⊗_R F→J give the full Hom model Hom_A(Q,J) of ΨΦ(L). The signed map l↦(q↦(−1)^(|q||l|)j(q⊗l)) is the actual unit for every unbounded L.

stages.label: The exact defect of passing from finite cells to the full source
stages.description: The actual unit is invertible on perfect R-modules. For any finite-cell presentation F=colim_T F_T, its cone is the tensor–Hom interchange defect. In every degree n and weight w it fits into 0→coker γ^(n,w)→Hⁿ(Cone η_L)_w→ker γ^(n+1,w)→0, where γ compares maps from W⟨w⟩ into the finite realized stages with maps into Φ(L).

stages.label: An explicit localization at the algebraic realization kernel
stages.description: For K_P=ker(P⊗ᴸ_R−), countable semifree null generators and an explicit ω₁ evaluation-cone tower construct the exact reflector λ_P:D(R)→K_P^⊥ on every ordinary unbounded input. Its kernel is exactly K_P, and it inverts exactly the derived P-tensor equivalences, giving D(R)/K_P≃K_P^⊥.

stages.label: The actual unit factors through the source reflector
stages.description: Under the native comparison UΦ≃P⊗ᴸ_R−, the algebraic kernel is ker Φ and every Ψ(M) is local. The actual unit factors uniquely as L→λ_P L —β_L→ ΨΦ(L), with β_L=(ΨΦ(ℓ_L))⁻¹η_(λ_P L). The adjunct of β_L is the inverse of Φ(ℓ_L).

stages.label: Both adjoints are conservative on the localized cellular comparison
stages.description: Under the native hypotheses, the actual adjunction restricts from K_P^⊥ to the full smooth derived category with conservative left adjoint. Restricting the target to C_W makes both adjoints conservative. The source reflector is universal among exact Verdier source localizations through which Φ factors conservatively.

stages.label: The unit defect has a kernel part and a local part
stages.description: Under the native hypotheses, Cone(ℓ_L)→Cone(η_L)→Cone(β_L)→Cone(ℓ_L)[1] is a distinguished triangle. Its first term is P-null, its third term is local, and applying λ_P to the unit cone gives Cone(β_L). For any P-null L, the actual unit is L→0 and its cone is L[1].

stages.label: The remaining unit on the localized source
stages.description: The construction removes exactly the realization kernel but does not prove β_L invertible for every local source. An equivalence between the localized source K_P^⊥ and C_W therefore remains outside this theorem, even though both adjoints are conservative.

readingPaths.title: Follow the smooth recipient
readingPaths.summary: Start with joint torsion and the unbounded cellular approximation. Compare torsion terms, bounded-below torsion cohomology, and the intrinsic torsion derived category before reading the actual counit criterion. This is an editorial route; only the displayed source relations are dependency edges.

stages.label: Finite affine cells for joint augmentation torsion
stages.description: For B=U(tg[t]) and its augmentation ideal I, the quotients B/Iʳ are finite-dimensional. The induced cells E_r=A⊗_B(B/Iʳ) have finite filtrations by shifts of the regular-top W. They make Γ_I(M)={v:Iʳv=0 for some r} an affine submodule and give the Grothendieck torsion category T.

stages.label: A cellular approximation for every unbounded smooth complex
stages.description: On the full ordinary unbounded smooth derived category, the explicit ω₁ tower of smooth K-injective replacements and quotients by Γ_I constructs Cell_I M→M→Null_I M. Cell_I is the exact coreflector onto C_W=Loc(W shifts), and Null_I is the exact reflector onto C_W^⊥. There is no cohomological or energy bound.

stages.label: Unbounded complexes with torsion terms are cellular
stages.description: Every actual complex whose terms are jointly I-torsion belongs to C_W, with no cohomological or energy bound. Internally, the ordinary derived category D(T) is generated by W and all required shifts. This objectwise assertion does not identify its morphisms with ambient derived morphisms.

stages.label: Cohomological torsion and cellularity agree when bounded below
stages.description: For cohomologically bounded-below smooth objects, membership in C_W is equivalent to joint I-torsion of every cohomology module. C_W is closed under both standard truncations and has heart T. Cell_I preserves D^(≥n) and has H⁰(Cell_I V)=Γ_I V on every smooth module V.

stages.label: The genuine unbounded derived torsion adjunction
stages.description: The exact functor i:D(T)→D(Sm(A)) has right adjoint RΓ_I, computed by applying Γ_I to a genuine smooth K-injective replacement. Its kernel is C_W^⊥, and its included output belongs to C_W. This derived torsion operator has not been identified with Cell_I.

stages.label: The unrestricted torsion-cohomology comparison
stages.description: The full equality D_I=C_W is equivalent to D_I∩ker(RΓ_I)=0. The cellularization theorem isolates this residual and proves it has no nonzero bounded-below objects, but does not prove that it vanishes on all unbounded objects.

stages.label: Comparing intrinsic and ambient torsion categories
stages.description: Full faithfulness and an essential-image description for D(T)→D(Sm(A)) remain outside these results. The operators iRΓ_I and Cell_I are not identified by the proof; neither their equality nor their inequality is established.

stages.label: The actual native counit factors through cellularization
stages.description: Under the coherent native adjunction, the actual counit factors uniquely as ΦΨM→Cell_I M→M, and Ψ sends the second map to an equivalence. The first map is invertible exactly when η_(ΨM) is invertible. Hence the actual counit is invertible exactly when M is cellular and that actual unit is invertible.

readingPaths.title: From the augmentation locus to one fixed character
readingPaths.summary: Start with the transverse augmentation locus, then distinguish the underlying critical maps. Read the zero-character family, the positive-source theorem and the exact Koszul restriction image before asking for a classification of the remaining components.

stages.label: The transverse augmentation locus
stages.description: For universal polynomial affine cochains of a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra with nondegenerate shifted form, the full ordered-atlas transverse monoid has a coherent unital augmentation through a connected space of choices. Its underlying mapping space is connected and simply connected, and every specified underlying map has a nonempty connected fibre of coherent lifts. For simple complex \(\mathfrak g\) at scalar level \(\ell\), the transverse augmentation space is nonempty exactly when \(\ell\ne-h^\vee\). Underlying critical coalgebra maps have their own nonempty mapping spaces after multiplication is forgotten.

stages.label: Critical underlying maps have no transverse lift
stages.description: For the universal polynomial affine cochain transverse monoid of a simple complex Lie algebra at \(\ell=-h^\vee\), the augmentation space is empty. The native degree-\((0,1)\) supported-pairing detector has nonzero highest normal vacuum coefficient \(h^\vee\dim(\mathfrak g)/2\). It excludes arbitrary full-envelope transverse augmentations, while leaving underlying coalgebra maps possible.

stages.label: Every fixed constant critical character occurs
stages.description: For every finite-dimensional simple complex Lie algebra at critical level and every fixed constant vector \(c\), an actual underlying coalgebra map \(\chi_c:C_Z\to J\) exists on the full ordered atlas. Its singleton degree-zero cohomology sends \(q_{i,0}\) to \(c_i\) and all positive central jets to zero. Different constant vectors determine different connected components.

stages.label: Distinct components with the same entire zero character
stages.description: For universal critical \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) cochains, let \(\mathcal M_0\) be the homotopy fibre of central singleton restriction over the entire differential-module map \(\epsilon_0:f(q_0,q_1,\ldots)\mapsto f(0,0,\ldots)\). There are actual full-atlas points \(\chi_t\in\mathcal M_0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb C\). At any two distinct positions, the invariant \(I_{x,y}(\chi_t)=-t\) is preserved by every admitted derived homotopy. Thus \(\mathbb C\) injects into \(\pi_0\mathcal M_0\), even though the entire central character is fixed.

stages.label: Positive sources have a connected full mapping space
stages.description: Let \(E=k\mathbf1\oplus M\) be a vacuum-split chiral \(L_\infty\) algebra on the affine line over a characteristic-zero field. If every \(M^d\) is free over \(k[T]\) and \(M^d=0\) for \(d<1\), with the canonical strict vacuum action, then the full derived space \(\operatorname{Map}_{J/\mathcal D}(C_E,J)\) is nonempty and connected. The scalar projection supplies a point. Arbitrary rank, an unbounded positive complex and all homotopy-coherent maps are included.

stages.label: The Koszul source reaches exactly one zero-character component
stages.description: Put \(W=Z\otimes\Lambda[\psi]\), with \(|\psi|=-1\) and \(D\psi=S\). The full mapping space \(\mathcal N=\operatorname{Map}_{J/\mathcal D}(C_W,J)\) is nonempty and connected. Restriction along the actual inclusion \(C_Z\to C_W\) has image on connected components equal to the single component of \(\chi_0\), which is also the component of the specified Koszul augmentation.

stages.label: What is still unknown about the critical mapping spaces?
stages.description: The displayed family and the image of Koszul restriction are determined. A classification of all components of the exact zero-character fibre remains separate, including whether vanishing of the binary invariant characterizes the Koszul component. Other central-character fibres, the full central-restriction image and higher homotopy groups are not classified by these results. The general positive-source mapping theorem gives connectedness, not contractibility.

readingPaths.note: This is an editorial reading order. It does not assert that successive items form a proof dependency chain.

readingPaths.title: Read the obstruction in its full domain
readingPaths.summary: Read the full Koszul recurrence before the binary detector. Then compare the nonzero first obstruction with the specified-point primitive and the precise scope of the simplified gauge formula.

stages.label: The full Koszul extension recurrence
stages.description: For a specified twisting cochain \(\tau\), write \(a=\tau\pi_0\), \(D_0=\partial_0+[a,-]\) and \(B=aQ_\delta\). An extension is a solution of \(B+D_0\theta+\kappa\theta+\theta^2=0\). In exterior weight \(m\), the equation is \(D_0\theta_m=-\mathbf1_{m=1}B-\kappa\theta_{m-1}-\sum_{i+j=m,\ i,j\ge1}\theta_i\theta_j\), with \(\theta_0=0\). Its first obstruction lies in the actual global \(H^2(K_1,D_0)\); later obstructions are closed once the lower equations hold.

stages.label: The binary test detects a genuine global obstruction
stages.description: After unary normalization, two-output evaluation descends to the full global group \(H^2(K_1,D_0)\) and kills every global boundary. For the actual point \(\chi_t\), it sends \([B_t]\) to \(t\operatorname{sym}(uv)\), where \(\operatorname{sym}(uv)=(uv+vu)/2\) uses the two unit-current entries at distinct positions. At the specified Koszul point, restriction of its actual full extension supplies a global primitive for its own first obstruction.

stages.label: The first global obstruction is nonzero for nonzero parameters
stages.description: For \(t\ne0\), the coefficient \(t\operatorname{sym}(uv)\) is nonzero, so \([B_t]\ne0\) in the genuine global first Koszul obstruction group. Higher corrections cannot remove this first obstruction. This independently identifies the obstruction behind the nonextension of the actual zero-character family.

stages.label: The full gauge equation and its binary specialization
stages.description: The twisted differential at the specified primitive-valued point retains scalar-output source operations, mixed vacuum inputs and every output action. It preserves PBW output number as a linear differential, while nonlinear deformations use the full envelope product. The simplified vacuum-free binary gauge change \(-\xi_1s\mu(a,\theta)\) has one output and leaves the two-output coefficient unchanged only in the strict heart-valued or normalized bounded local operator model. A general dg operator resolution retains its operator boundary and exact unary terms until normalization.

stages.label: Global primitives would assemble without completing states
stages.description: If actual global primitives solve the Koszul recurrence at every exterior weight, they assemble into a full extension. Each algebraic state has finite exterior degree and each fixed configuration has finitely many contributing blocks. This assembly result does not assert that arbitrary obstruction classes vanish.
